data.title: French student protests: Police impunity ‘below' the standards of a 'well-functioning democracy’
data.description: Erin Ogunkeye welcomes Dr. Antoine Marie, postdoctoral researcher, fellow and lecturer at Sciences Po / CEVIPOF, to explore the political psychology behind France’s student protests. Why do people witness the same events yet reach radically different conclusions about violence? Dr Marie examines how media echo chambers, partisan thinking and the politicization of empathy deepen polarization, making it easier to overlook the suffering of those perceived as political opponents. He also examines France’s increasingly offensive police doctrine, questions surrounding accountability, and the institutional incentives that may actually hinder independent investigations into police misconduct.

They discuss grandchildren, swimming with turtles and who shot JFK ‘Earmuffs!” says Sam Rockwell, pausing his gushing tribute mid-flow and turning to face John Malkovich on the couch. Rockwell loves Malkovich and has been discussing his work at some length. Malkovich, he says, is charismatic and dangerous, half masculine, half feminine; a unique combination and the perfect sparring partner. He’s one of the world’s finest actors and annoyingly modest to boot. “Earmuffs!” says Rockwell and pivots back towards me. “He hates hearing all this. That’s why I keep saying ‘earmuffs’.” Malkovich frowns. “I don’t mind it,” he says. Continue reading...

data.title: Experience: I became the world’s oldest crowd surfer at 99
data.description: After retiring at 83, I had a new lease of life creating social media content with my grandson. Then I broke the crowd surfing world record In 2013, aged 87, I was playing basketball with my grandson Ross in Ohio while he was home from college. He made a video of me blocking his shot, posted it online, and people really ate it up. We started doing comedy skits together and now have more than 4 million followers on Instagram. After doing lots of short videos, we decided to make a documentary about my life. As part of it, we compiled my bucket list. One of the things I wanted to do was break a world record. Ross and I spent months thinking of something that would be outrageous, but also fun and inclusive. We settled on me becoming the world’s oldest crowd surfer. Continue reading...

data.title: Troye Sivan: She’s the Best review – a strange, singular pop star who deserves to be multiplatinum
data.description: (Interscope) Adored by the A-list and filling arenas, but without huge smash hits, the Australian singer treads his own distinctive path through pop via shoegaze, Balearic and the Smiths A few years back, the New York Times reported on the phenomenon of the “middle-class pop star”. The feature bluntly explained that this signified “a pop star who isn’t that popular”, for whom the word signified not commercial dominance, but “a sound, an aesthetic, an attitude”. It isn’t an entirely new phenomenon: you may recall a game late 00s attempt to differentiate critically acclaimed but commercially underground pop artists – Alphabeat, Frankmusik and the Clik Clik among them – from the massed ranks of chart-topping TV talent show graduates by grouping them together under the generic banner of “wonky pop”. But the arrival of social media clearly changed things dramatically, enabling artists who seldom, if ever, encroach on the charts’ upper reaches to develop ferociously loyal – and very online – followings, reliably packed-out shows and a genuine aura of celebrity to go with their good reviews. Troye Sivan might well be the apotheosis of this phenomenon. Over the last 12 years, his albums have shifted respectable, rather than earth-shattering quantities. Intermittently, the odd single has become a mainstream hit, but their success is vastly outstripped by his profile – arena tours, features in broadsheet newspapers and style magazines, interviews on late night US chatshows – and indeed his standing among huge stars. He has been glowingly written about in Time magazine by Kylie Minogue. Nicole Kidman appears in the video for the title track from She’s the Best. Madonna apparently gave personal approval for him to use a sample from 2000’s Music on another of the album’s singles, Party. He has duetted on hits by Dua Lipa, Ariana Grande and Charli xcx, with whom he co-headlined a US tour just after the release of Brat. Continue reading...

data.title: Willem de Kooning review – the artist’s lifelong rebellion against himself is thrilling to watch
data.description: Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam Marking a century since the Dutch artist stowed away to New York, this vast retrospective gloriously showcases the abstract expressionist’s fierce boundary-pushing Willem de Kooning was the last great artist who really knew how to draw. More precisely, if less provocatively, he was the last truly transformative painter to have been schooled in the academic tradition that produces what is still recognised, by most people, as “good drawing”. Accurate in the sense of a photograph but, like a filter on your cameraphone, also subtly tidying up the world to meet the ideals of classical proportion. “Draw what you see and not what you think,” the young De Kooning was told. Raw personal emotion had no place – a far cry from what this master of abstract expressionism was to become. The intense labour required to build a connection between eye, brain and hand so quick as to be instinctive is illustrated by the charcoal still life Dish With Jugs. Made when De Kooning was in his mid-teens, and so minutely rendered that you might mistake it for a sepia photograph, the catalogue estimates that it took 600 hours at the Rotterdam academy to complete. The aim of this exercise was not to produce a single picture so much as to ingrain a way of seeing and reconstructing the world to the point that it becomes inescapable. Continue reading...

data.title: Pentagon says execution of Fort Hood shooter will be livestreamed

A defense department official later confirmed the execution will be livestreamed. In an interview with Real America’s Voice, the Pentagon secretary said the firing squad will carry out the sentence at Fort Hood, Texas, at 1pm on Thursday, 3 December. This would be the first US military execution in more than 60 years. Continue reading...

Greens will be there every single day, holding Labour to account and demanding the change people voted for. Continue reading...

data.title: Animals crossing: the simple solution to stop roadkill in the Amazon
data.description: Installation of eight canopy bridges in Alta Floresta has enabled 15,000 safe crossings by animals including spider monkeys and marmosets – and more bridges are planned elsewhere By about 7am, with dense fog blanketing the landscape, Gabriel Falquetto had already come across several road-killed animals along the ES-164 highway in Brazil’s Espírito Santo state. The biologist was on his way to Kaetés private natural heritage reserve (RPPN) in the Atlantic Forest, where he monitors wildlife and roadkill. Then he spotted the lifeless body of a primate on the pavement. It was a buffy-headed marmoset ( Callithrix flaviceps ), a species listed as critically endangered on the International Union for Conservation of Nature red list. An estimated 2,500 individuals remain in the wild, making it one of the world’s most threatened primates. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘Is death necessary?’: why Peter Greenaway’s assisted dying drama is stuck in post-production hell
data.description: Exclusive: Three years after filming began on the contentious Lucca Mortis, starring Dustin Hoffman, the British director is still in dispute with producers over which version to release, and a battle over rights rumbles on Peter Greenaway’s new movie was supposed to mark a glorious swansong for him and his lead actor Dustin Hoffman, the Oscar-winning star of The Graduate and Tootsie. Both men were in their 80s when shooting began in Lucca, Tuscany, in late 2023. Neither knew the storms ahead or that this was going to turn into arguably the most troublesome project in Greenaway’s career. Turn the clock back to 2023 and Greenaway, who has been based in the Netherlands for the last 20 years, could hardly conceal his excitement during a Q&A at International Documentary Film Festival Amsterdam (IDFA) in the huge art deco Tuschinski theatre in Amsterdam in November 2023, after receiving a lifetime achievement award from the festival. He told the audience that he would be flying to Italy the next morning “and that, all being well, we will start shooting seriously in the next couple of days”. Continue reading...

data.title: The Queerest of Folk by Russell T Davies review – the groundbreaking screenwriter tells it like it is
data.description: From Coronation Street to It’s a Sin, Davies’ memoir of a career in TV is also a rallying cry for creativity Television is an intimate art form, once beamed into living rooms, now on devices right in front of our faces. The screenwriter Russell T Davies understands that intimacy. Whether discussing his early days developing lost-to-history soap spin-offs, making a splash with the pioneering gay series Queer As Folk , or reviving Doctor Who to great acclaim, he makes it feel as if you’re at the pub with him, settling in for the night, ready to hear his best stories. This warm and gossipy autobiography offers a peek behind the curtains of the British TV industry, and as such, it goes light on Davies’s own life story. Instead, he gallops through five decades in the business, using the framework of his TV shows to propel the book forward at great speed. He was born in Swansea in 1963, to a family who loved watching TV. While he was studying English at Oxford, a friend suggested that, as he thought television was so great, he should consider doing it as his job. Continue reading...

data.title: You have a higher chance of getting cancer at a younger age than your parents. So what went wrong? | Devi Sridhar
data.description: Some change in our lifestyles and environments over a generation has caused this increased risk. What, exactly, is a mystery Prof Devi Sridhar is chair of global public health at the University of Edinburgh In the field of global health, we often talk about each generation living longer and healthier lives than their parents. We’ve seen this in the gains in life expectancy, the sharp decrease in child mortality and in the near elimination of many vaccine-preventable diseases. But since the turn of the century this progress has stalled, and in some cases several health metrics have gone backwards. Take cancer, which was long thought to be a disease linked to old age. While most cancers do indeed still occur in elderly people, a new report highlights that a number of cancers are increasing in people who are under 50 , often referred to as “early onset cancer”. The report, undertaken by the World Cancer Research Fund, looked at data from 12 different cancer types in England, the US and the Netherlands over the past 20 years. What they found isn’t pretty. Prof Devi Sridhar is chair of global public health at the University of Edinburgh Continue reading...

data.title: How do human beings rationalize genocide? NAZA provides a chilling look | Omer Bartov
data.description: It’s easier to blame brutes and sadists for extreme violence. But as we see in the documentary, modern genocides are fueled by people who are uncomfortably recognizable Werner Best, a senior SS official and jurist who helped organize the Nazi death squads that murdered hundreds of thousands of Jews, is also known for his statement: “We must destroy the enemy without hating him.” He belonged to a younger generation of Nazi technocrats, who despised the foul-mouthed, beer-bellied, brown-shirted “old fighters” of the Nazi party in the 1920s, and believed in organizing genocide neatly and dispassionately. After the fall of the regime, Best escaped justice for the rest of his long life, dying peacefully in Germany in 1989. His chilling statement came to my mind while I was watching the film NAZA. I grew up in Tel Aviv and have visited there often in recent years. That is why the interviews with 24 Israeli soldiers and intelligence officers, which make up this documentary, felt strangely familiar. The conversations are conducted at night on rooftops, and the camera scans the cityscape, lingering on apartment windows as their inhabitants watch TV and make dinner. The landscape was intimately recognizable, and I felt a natural affinity with those people living their lives. I also recognized the way the interviewees talked – their speech patterns and choice of words. They reminded me of my son, who served more than a decade ago in the intelligence unit many of them might have belonged to. Continue reading...

data.title: A promising future now looks perilous for election loser Zack Polanski. He sowed, now he reaps | John Harris
data.description: There was a real chance of a Green byelection win in Holborn and St Pancras. He made bad decisions and cost his party dear As ever, among all the noise triggered by Labour holding the seat of Holborn and St Pancras , the most plain-spoken and undeniable analysis was provided by that sage and national treasure John Curtice, of Strathclyde University. The result, he said, echoed national opinion polls and reflected two undeniable facts: that the Greens are in need of a period of contrition and reflection, and Labour ought to be slightly less than ecstatic. Andy Burnham’s party, with a majority of 3,364, he said, showed they “are in a much better position than they were six months ago, but still not as popular as they were in 2025”. The Greens, meanwhile, remain “a more significant player than historically they have ever been”, but have lost much of the ground they gained during Zack Polanski’s first year as leader, when the serial failures of the local MP – one Keir Starmer – provided him and his party with such a glorious succession of political opportunities. John Harris is a Guardian columnist Continue reading...

data.title: British households would be £5,000 richer if we were more innovative. Let’s unleash our talents | Gordon Brown
data.description: We have a deep reservoir of assets, but struggle to turn small companies into global success stories. Innovation needs to be at the heart of government policy Gordon Brown was UK prime minister from 2007 to 2010 The coming 10 years are almost certain to be the decade that sees the greatest scientific breakthroughs in a century. The question is whether advances now under way in AI, quantum computing and biology can address cancer, find ways to treat or prevent dementia, and overcome the growing resistance to antibiotics. Can we find sustainable ways to address our energy needs and protect the environment at the same time? Can AI transform the way we deliver education, health and social care to the benefit of millions, as well as advance modern manufacturing strength? And what role can Britain’s inventors, investors and industrialists play in developing these transformative technologies? While the US and China are the world’s obvious innovation powerhouses, the UK also has enormous assets, as the Innovation Nation Conference in Manchester addressed by the prime minister, Andy Burnham, will hear today. We are home to four of the world’s top 10 universities and 16 of the top 100, five of which are in Europe’s top 10 for spin-outs, startups based on intellectual property produced through a university’s research. With less than 1% of the world’s population, the UK produces 6% of the world’s research papers, nearly 9% of citations and 12% of the most highly cited research. data.title: The Guardian view on cancers in under-50s: the risks of obesity must be confronted | Editorial
data.description: More research into the troubling rise in early onset cancers is needed. But we already know that food is among the culprits The latest findings about the rise in cancers in people under 50 , from the World Cancer Research Fund (WCRF), are extremely concerning. While a cancer diagnosis is bad news at any time, it is a particular blow for those in younger age groups where most people are in good health. Overlapping trends observed in England, the Netherlands and the US include a troubling rise in the incidence of colorectal (or bowel) cancer. Other diseases that have increased in England include uterine and kidney cancers. These diseases are still rare in young people: 10 times more adults in their 50s, 60s and 70s are diagnosed than those in their 20s, 30s and 40s. Earlier detection is thought to be one factor behind the rise in younger patients. Diagnosing more cancers sooner is an explicit policy goal in England, where late diagnosis and lower uptake of screening are two reasons for mortality rates that are higher than elsewhere in Europe. Continue reading...

data.title: The Guardian view on Ethiopia’s return to conflict: civilian catastrophe and a spiralling regional polycrisis | Editorial
data.description: The escalating violence reflects deep domestic rifts – but is fuelled by broader geopolitical power games When the Nobel peace laureate is announced on Friday, the committee will be hoping that its choice ages better than 2019’s. Ethiopia’s prime minister, Abiy Ahmed, won the prize for ending the 20-year border conflict with neighbouring Eritrea – signing a peace agreement with President Isaias Afwerki. A year later, their new relationship facilitated a war with the Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF) that killed as many as 600,000 people, displaced millions more, led to atrocities by both sides, and pushed Tigrayans into famine . Both sides bear responsibility for failing to properly implement the deal that ended that conflict in 2022, and the African Union and US did little to ensure that a piece of paper became a durable settlement. Now violence has resurged in northern Ethiopia, and old foes are forming bizarre new pacts. Last month, seven Ethiopian regional groups announced an “Alliance for Survival” to remove the federal government. Mr Abiy’s coalition is held together by his patronage, but so far may be faring better than his rivals, united solely by shared loathing of him and riven by deep disputes. The TPLF, which controls Tigray, has previously battled the Fano militia of Amhara, and their territorial dispute endures. Ethiopia accuses Eritrea – previously accused of atrocities against Tigrayan civilians – of backing the rebel alliance. Despite Asmara’s denials, there are multiple reports of Eritrean troops in Tigray . Continue reading...

Mr Abiy’s coalition is held together by his patronage, but so far may be faring better than his rivals, united solely by shared loathing of him and riven by deep disputes. The TPLF, which controls Tigray, has previously battled the Fano militia of Amhara, and their territorial dispute endures. Ethiopia accuses Eritrea – previously accused of atrocities against Tigrayan civilians – of backing the rebel alliance. Despite Asmara’s denials, there are multiple reports of Eritrean troops in Tigray . Continue reading...

data.title: Sergio Camello: ‘Rayo is the last team standing – it’s football from another time’
data.description: Rayo Vallecano’s fascinating forward on his unique club, his musical passions and the goalscoring form that puts him among Europe’e elite An 11-year-old, second-hand VW Beetle with more than 300,000km on the clock pulls over on Fofó the Clown Street in the heart of Vallecas. The music goes off, the Smiths silenced and out gets Sergio Camello: movie aficionado with 156 films reviewed , part-time photographer , sometime drummer, Olympic gold medallist and the second-top goalscorer in Europe’s biggest five leagues. Engulfed in graffiti, stickers covering the glass between metal bars in red, a single step up from the street, the small door into Rayo Vallecano’s ground is locked, but in 64 hours it will open for the first time this season. “It’s my home, it’s Vallecas,” Camello says. Forced to abandon their place, on Saturday at 2pm the tenants return. With the Madrid council declaring Estadio de Vallecas unsafe, unfit for purpose, Rayo’s home matches have instead been played in Leganés, out of the city to the south and boycotted by fans. Walking the neighbourhood that is proud of its social conscience, its community and its team, Camello can’t wait to be back again. And not just for the football; maybe not even for the football. “It’s the pre-game, the post-game, the people,” he says, passing the bar where they’ll be waiting for him after, same as always. Continue reading...

data.title: Oliver Glasner: ‘There was no plan for me to be Nottingham Forest manager’
data.description: On Sunday, Austrian returns to Crystal Palace, the club he left in the summer after leading them to unprecedented success, but accepts there could be ‘booing’ Oliver Glasner puffs his cheeks and starts the search for the right words to explain his emotions as he prepares to return to Crystal Palace for the first time since leaving. There is the small matter of heading back on Sunday with Nottingham Forest to Selhurst Park, where bitterness runs deep over the club seizing Palace’s place in the Europa League last season. Forest’s owner, Evangelos Marinakis, is suing Palace for defamation relating to a banner unfurled by their supporters and the rivalry heightened when Glasner joined Forest in the summer, 40 days after winning the Conference League with Palace. “I know I will be, but I don’t want to be in the middle of all the comments and the stories about this game,” he says in the boardroom at Forest’s training base. By which point Glasner, a charismatic and intelligent individual who studied for an economics degree while a player in Austria, has turned to Faust, by the German writer Johann Wolfgang von Goethe, to explain how he feels about facing his previous club. “Two hearts are beating in my chest,” he says, tapping his torso, alluding to a line in the classic play. “Here is a little bit similar, because we had a little bit more than two great years [at Palace].” Continue reading...

data.title: An elderly woman’s death after eviction is rocking Spain. Will public outcry help its socialist PM stay in power?
data.description: Recent death of 87-year-old woman likely to focus attention on crisis in run-up to election at end of November Even before María del Carmen Abascal died on Wednesday night , a mere fortnight after her eviction from the Madrid flat where she had lived for most of her life, the frail 87-year-old woman had become the enduring face of Spain’s housing crisis. Her plight – and the wider issue it embodied – had led to street demonstrations, the creation of a protest camp in the middle of the Spanish capital , and spurred the socialist-led government to propose emergency measures to facilitate and protect access to housing. When rightwing and far-right parties voted down those measures in congress last week, the prime minister, Pedro Sánchez, responded by announcing a snap general election for the end of November. Last week, Egyptian authorities arrested the journalists, from the independent factchecking and investigative platform Matsadaash, accusing them in a statement of being unlicensed and producing false news on behalf of the outlawed Muslim Brotherhood . data.title: Astronomers detect mysterious burst of energy from a galaxy far, far away
data.description: Intense flash of radio waves is more than 10bn years old and has travelled through ‘approximately 80% of cosmic history’ A long time ago in a galaxy far, far away, a mysterious flash of energy was released into the universe. Astronomers have now detected that flash – a burst of radio waves which travelled for more than 10bn years before reaching Earth – what they believe to be the most distant fast radio burst (FRB) ever recorded. data.title: Israel promotes film that mimics NAZA documentary
data.description: Embassies post links to hastily produced online film echoing style of real Guardian documentary about mass killings of Gaza civilians The Israeli government is promoting an online film project that mimics the style of NAZA, the award-winning documentary that details Israel’s mass killings of civilians in Gaza, in an attempt to counter the real film’s findings. The real documentary , directed by the Oscar-winning film-makers Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor, and produced by the Guardian, is in cinemas and will be shown in more than 50 countries. data.title: AK Blakemore: ‘The Goldfinch by Donna Tartt was extremely silly and bad’
data.description: The poet and author on F Scott Fitzgerald’s perfect novel, losing faith in Ernest Hemingway – and the recent debut that blew her away My earliest reading memory Lynley Dodd’s Hairy Maclary from Donaldson’s Dairy – where an assortment of differently shaped dogs go on a walk – wormed its way into my subconscious when I was very young. The great dane (Hercules Morse, as big as a horse), the dalmatian (Bottomley Potts, covered in spots), the dachshund (Schnitzel Von Krumm with a very low tum) … I could probably still recite most of it from memory. My favourite book growing up I had a lot of picture books illustrated by the great Korky Paul, and remember being obsessed – even as quite a young child – with the intricate grotesquerie of it all. He’s probably best known these days for illustrating the Winnie the Witch books, but my favourite was The Rascally Cake by Jeanne Willis, in which a rotund, green-haired man called Rufus Skumskins O’Parsley makes a cake out of disgusting things (rotten eggs, spider legs, garden snails and so on), only for the cake to come to life and attempt to eat him . Probably more than a little bit of Skumskins found its way into the protagonist of my second novel, The Glutton. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘Me and the lads would not survive a day in here’: inside TV’s utterly stunning, Bafta-winning prison drama
data.description: The third series of Jimmy McGovern’s breathtaking series Time stars David Tennant – and might just be its best ever. We go behind the scenes “I don’t think you would find a young offender institution (YOI) in which stories like these haven’t happened. Seventeen years of age, loads of energy, hormones, bravado – you know they’ll kick off. It must be an absolute nightmare.” Yes, Jimmy McGovern has gone back to prison again. After two series of Time, which told stories from men’s and women’s institutions , he has turned his attention to perhaps the most distressing ones of all. Set in a YOI, it’s full of tales of bad decisions, directionless rage and lost potential at the most vulnerable of ages. If this third series is, as he suggests, the last, it is quite the curtain call. Continue reading...

data.title: Matchbox: the Movie review – as pointless as a film based on a toy car could be
data.description: John Cena and Jessica Biel collect paychecks in a soulless and synthetic slab of corporate product that hints at what we can expect from the Paramount-Warner merger After a windy road, this week it finally happened . The day that Hollywood, and many of those who are invested in it, had been dreading, the grimly inevitable disappearance of Warner Bros as it was consumed by what is now known as Paramount. The two once-classic studios will become one – Skydance, the David Ellison-owned company that has infinitely more money than common sense or base-level creativity. The week has seen many, including the Guardian , speculate about what we may be able to expect, what kind of films the billion-dollar behemoth might now be releasing. Warners after all has created classics such as Casablanca, The Exorcist and 2001: A Space Odyssey while Paramount has been behind The Godfather, Chinatown and Breakfast at Tiffany’s. Just imagine what the combined might of these two prestigious, industry-defining studios could achieve with the promise of 30-plus theatrical releases a year, huge amounts of money and considerable manpower at play. Continue reading...

data.title: Lourdes gets a Vegas glow-up at Dublin theatre festival, where canvases are slashed
data.description: A musical about a drama group’s pilgrimage and reflections on activist art join an intriguing show about lost languages In a Dublin theatre festival programme tackling heavy themes of racism, conflict and prejudice, Lourdes! The Musical ( ★★★★☆ ) promises something effervescent. Xnthony Ltd , the creators of Oliver Cromwell Is Really Very Sorry , have turned their lightly quizzical gaze to the French pilgrimage town – “a holy Blackpool, a divine Las Vegas” and a site of hope or desperation for five unlikely travelling companions. Back in his home village in “Countryland”, in 2008, following a diagnosis of HIV that punctures his dreams of Los Angeles, singer-songwriter Matthew (Riain Cash) lends his star power to a parish drama group taking a musical about Saint Bernadette to Lourdes. Interweaving this show-within-a-show and the pilgrimage strands, Xnthony’s lyrics and Matthew Floyd Jones’s score blend pop, club beats and soulful ballads. Directed by Sarah Meadows, the supercharged ensemble joining Cash as, variously, a droll priest (Iestyn Arwel), a terminally ill mother and her transgender daughter (Nichola MacEvilly and Danielle James) and an eager tour manager (Molly Lynch) carry the music’s tonal shifts effortlessly. Continue reading...

data.title: Branford Marsalis Quartet and Dianne Reeves: Dedicated to You review – eloquent Coltrane tribute
data.description: (Blue Note) This elegant contemporary reinvention of 1963 album John Coltrane and Johnny Hartman pairs Marsalis’s post-bop sax with Reeves’ agile vocals, to time-stopping effect In the early 1960s, the Impulse! label tried to steer its star saxophonist John Coltrane away from increasingly uncompromising and experimental music that it feared might be scaring its customers. Label boss Bob Thiele suggested a more palatable all-ballads album with a little-known African American supper-club singer called Johnny Hartman, whose warm, Bing Crosby-like baritone but bracing absence of schmaltz had already impressed Frank Sinatra and Tony Bennett. Coltrane and Hartman hit it off perfectly, and the 1963 album, John Coltrane and Johnny Hartman, was an unexpected mini masterpiece of restraint, flawless timbral expressiveness, and mutual understanding. Invited by Blue Note Records in Coltrane’s centenary year to curate his own tribute, post-bop sax luminary Branford Marsalis made that album the template for Dedicated to You – done as contemporary reinventions, not mere cover versions. Marsalis invited Dianne Reeves, a vastly experienced jazz singer with a Sarah Vaughan-like mix of flawless intonation and agile spontaneity, to take the vocal role. “Listening to all the great singers coming up”, Reeves has said, “I learned that they stood in the band, not in front of the band. They saw themselves as co-creators of the sound.” Continue reading...

data.title: Jess Williamson: A Mile South of Heaven review – alt-country singer’s love-hate affair with LA
data.description: (New West) Following 2023 breakout Time Ain’t Accidental, the best songs here are when Williamson strips back country music, rebuilding it as something familiar yet different In her essay Goodbye to All That , Joan Didion writes that she left New York City when “the golden rhythm was broken”. Texas-born alt-country singer Jess Williamson borrows the title for the aching opening track of her sixth solo album, on which she contemplates whether she has had enough of Los Angeles. But while Didion was looking back on leaving the city of her youth behind, Williamson is still in LA, wrestling with competing desires to stay or flee. This tumultuous love-me, love-me-not is set to Williamson’s most traditional soundscapes to date: “Deep in the woods I feel the hum of the city,” she sings on Hum of the City in her strongest Texas drawl over mournful strings and twiddling banjo. Gone are the iPhone-programmed drums that made her 2023 breakout Time Ain’t Accidental so appealingly offbeat, and while the Americana flourishes give weight to Williamson’s nostalgia for her native Dallas, at times they make the album stodgier and less imaginative than her previous record. Continue reading...

data.title: Shostakovich Symphony No 8 album review – composer’s cry of despair in a remarkable and resonant new recording
data.description: Frankfurt Radio Symphony/Altinoglu (Alpha) Conductor Alain Altinoglu brings weight and purpose while the instrumental solos are piquant and precise. If the Leningrad was Shostakovich’s official response to the second world war, the Eighth Symphony was his answer to the question: “Will you tell us what you really think?” Written while the fighting was still under way, its immediacy remains striking today, a quality reflected in Alain Altinoglu’s purposeful interpretation with the Frankfurt Radio Symphony orchestra. You hear that directness at once in the way the strings dig deep, bringing remarkable colours to a 26-minute Adagio that, in the wrong hands, can sound merely bleak and black. Not that Altinoglu shuns the horrors: his phrasing and textural dynamics bring fearsome weight and a sense of wide-eyed terror to the composer’s protracted cry of despair. The orchestra covers itself in glory with instrumental solos that are piquant and precise. Resonant details are captured by an outstanding German production team that manages to outdo the Berlin Philharmonic’s excellent 2020 account under Kirill Petrenko (Shostakovich fans will need both). Continue reading...

data.title: End Of Abyss review – a creepy dollhouse take on Resident Evil and The Thing
data.description: PlayStation 5 (version played), Xbox, PC; Epic Games Publishing This fetchingly presented horror game brings style and scares, but overextends itself with repetition A small band of soldiers enters an abandoned facility, where puckered flesh sprouts from cold steel. It’s a promising but familiar start to a sci-fi horror story, with heavy overtones of Alien and The Thing. Neither of those, though, were so … dinky. End of Abyss’s facility is presented as a kind of a model-village recreation of The Thing’s Outpost 31 that you peer into from above. Your little bobble-headed hero takes up a tiny fraction of the screen, with most of the remainder drenched in foggy darkness, or even blanked out entirely. This is a world of Usborne-style cutaways, where anything outside the walls is total blackness. Continue reading...

data.title: Sofia Coppola: ‘I’m glad we weren’t kicked out of Tokyo making Lost in Translation’
data.description: The director talks about what she learnt from her mother, working with a rookie Tim Burton, and 20 years of her cult classic Marie Antoinette Hello , I’m Cherry, I’m 14 and an aspiring film-maker. I love how your films capture what it feels like to be a young girl growing up. We hear so much about the famous men in your family, but how have the successful women in your family inspired and influenced you? Your films capture the experience of what it is to be a young girl in a way words often can’t. CherryEmma That’s nice to hear, thank you. I feel like I got a lot from my mom about being true to yourself, following what you’re interested in and seeing the beauty in your surroundings. My mom always noticed odd details in life, so a lot of my films are made up of those kinds of things. Your films beautifully capture the isolation of hotel rooms – spaces completely detached from a character’s past or future. If you were forced into that stillness and could choose to preserve only one cherished memory while erasing another for ever, what would they be? Malpractice1 It’s hard to pick a memory, but recently we had a party in Versailles for the anniversary of Marie Antoinette and New Order played. When they started playing Ceremony [from the soundtrack] and the lights went on, I just know that in the future when I have to remember a happy memory, that’s going to be it. Even painful memories are part of making you who you are, and you learn from them, so I can’t think of anything I would erase. Continue reading...

data.title: Good night, and good lick: what can we expect from George Clooney’s restaurant?
data.description: The newly-official French citizen is planning to open an Italian restaurant in Provence. Will it float like his tequila brand or sink as swiftly as the Steven Spielberg submarine eatery that made one reviewer ‘embarrassed to be human’? The Provençal village of Cotignac is not wanting for places to eat. Within a short drive of its pale stone houses, you can find a wealth of high-end dining options. La Table de Mentone, set within the beautiful Château Mentone wine estate, is famed for the produce it grows on site. The Michelin-starred Restaurant Bruno offers dazzling variations of truffle dishes. More locally, Picotte Provence offers the sort of charming village dining that showcases the best of what the region has to offer. However, despite all these wonderful options, there is one thing that Cotignac does not yet boast, and that’s a celebrity vanity project. But that is all about to change, thanks to the news that George Clooney is planning to open a restaurant there. Continue reading...

data.title: Rent review – Jonathan Larson’s New York bohos move into the West End and unpack their passions
data.description: Tom Stoppard theatre, London Stranger Things’ Gaten Matarazzo leads the grief-stricken 90s musical about friends living under the threat of Aids Is Rent one of the musical greats? It’s a forever fan favourite – this new production extended its run even before the official opening – and its origin story holds a special place in theatre-kid hearts. Jonathan Larson , Rent’s creator, died just before the off-Broadway premiere in 1996, aged 35 – a poignant echo of its raggle-taggle bohemians in New York, living fast and fearing death will come before their time. This production is developed by director Luke Sheppard ( Paddington: The Musical ) from his version at Manchester’s Hope Mill theatre . With onstage seating circling the space, Sheppard cradles the piece in community, knitting together the story’s hopeful vagabonds. data.title: The woman with the mattress: the radical, rage-fuelled history of anti-rape art
data.description: A performance piece from 2014 has gone viral in response to an allegation of rape at Cornell University. But with such defiant pieces stretching back hundreds of years, will things ever change? In September 2014, Emma Sulkowicz began to carry a blue mattress weighing 23kg around her university campus. The mattress was similar to the ones New York’s Columbia University used in its dorm rooms, where Sulkowicz said she had been raped by a fellow student two years earlier. Her performance/endurance artwork constituted her visual art senior thesis, drawing attention to the lack of criminal charges brought against her alleged attacker and his continued presence at the university. As she hauled it across campus, others could choose to assist her with her burden. Many did. She recorded responses to the piece in a diary. “I could have taken my pillow,” she told the writer Jessica Valenti at the time. “But I want people to see how it weighs down a person to be ignored by the school administration and harassed by police.” Sulkowicz would carry the mattress , she said, for as long as her alleged attacker remained at Columbia. And so she ended up carrying it all the way to graduation where, helped by other women, she took it on stage. The university president refused to shake her hand, turning away from her instead. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘My dog’s built her own fashion community’: how canine companions stole the fashion week spotlight
data.description: Our four-legged friends are turning heads from Louis Vuitton to Schiaparelli – but what does their presence in the most exclusive of spaces say about the industry’s changing attitudes? • Don’t get Fashion Statement delivered to your inbox? Sign up here The front row at a fashion week show is a known hotspot for celebrities. During the most recent iteration that wrapped up on Tuesday, sightings included Heathcliff, AKA Jacob Elordi, high-fiving the Adolescence star Owen Cooper at Bottega Veneta; Rihanna arriving 63 minutes late to the Matières Fécales show; and Dua Lipa gossiping with Nicole Kidman and Pedro Pascal at Chanel. But peppered in among the Hollywood crowd was another type of guest going head-to-head for the photographers’ attention: dogs. From a cavapoo at Louis Vuitton to a shih tzu at Schiaparelli, four-legged companions – rather than designer bags – sat on the laps of many showgoers. At the Balenciaga show, Brooklyn Beckham and Nicole Peltz sat next to Miranda Priestly – no, not Meryl Streep in her Devil Wears Prada character, but the brand’s creative director Pierpaolo Piccioli’s rescue dog. Tommy Hilfiger took his post-show bow with a fluffy samoyed – a look-a-like of Travis Kelce and Taylor Swift’s pup who stars with Kelce in a campaign for the brand. Elsewhere, a miniature schnauzer in goggles and a chihuahua wearing a puffer jacket took over the catwalk at Chopova Lowena. Continue reading...

data.title: Benjamina Ebuehi’s recipe for toffee apple Basque cheesecake | The sweet spot
data.description: A crisp surface and creamy core are the traits of this cheesecake with no base, here topped with spiced and sliced apples and a sticky, caramel sauce My go-to cheesecake these days is a burnt Basque. It’s so good it doesn’t even need a biscuit base, which might be the very reason some people aren’t fans. But Basque cheesecakes are rarely too sweet, because the burnt top provides just enough bitterness to balance things out and the insides stay ridiculously creamy. If I can give you one tip, though, it’s to make sure you take it out of the oven while it’s still really wobbly, to get the best set. An overbaked Basque is no fun at all. Continue reading...

data.title: SOS meals – the food to cook for friends that shows you care
data.description: After the death of my beloved dog, I’m thinking a lot about the role food plays in all of life’s big events – be they happy or sad • Sign up here for our weekly food newsletter, Feast I lost my beloved cairn terrier Wilf a couple of weeks ago, and when I say lost, sadly, I don’t mean I mislaid him yet again on Hampstead Heath. Rather, after 13 and a half years of (mostly) civil disobedience, we had to make the tough but ultimately kind decision to say a final goodbye. Since then, I have been bombarded with kindness. Friends and family have rallied round to take me out for breakfast, lunch, dinner and coffee, clearly worried that the bereavement might affect my appetite – well, apart from the one who responded by having a baby a week early, and who now requires me to provide for her. It got me thinking about the part food plays in big life events. We so often cook, or otherwise provide for people in the aftermath of such shocks, be they happy or sad, as a way both to offer practical help and to show them how much we love them. Such tokens of affection tend to fall into two camps. The first is high-energy food that can be easily eaten with one hand while the other is holding a baby or clutching a sodden handkerchief, or simply when you’re just too busy to sit down. Just this morning, I received a picture of the new mother tucking into my extremely wholesome fruit and nut-packed granola with her daughter sleeping on her arm, but Melissa Hemsley’s five-ingredient flapjacks (pictured top) would fall into this category, as would Meera Sodha’s chaat masala popcorn and Thomasina Miers’ dark chocolate and toasted walnut banana bread . Like Anna Jones’s chocolate chip cookie power bites , Hugh Fearnley-Whittingstall’s spiced nuts or my own kale chips , they’re full of good things, and tempting enough to compete with the less nutritious options that are so easy to reach for instead. (That said, no one should judge anyone for the choices they make at times of stress.) Continue reading...

data.title: Cold comforts: the most satisfying autumn whites
data.description: As summer fades and our social and dining habits adapt to the cooling weather, so, too, should the white wine we drink. Here are some options best-suited to the season The wine world is full of clubs, and I’m a member of the Just-Drink-What-You-Bloody-Like club, which makes even the thought of white wines for autumn and winter feel uncomfortably prescriptive. But, for me, as the nights draw in, there’s less standing, more sitting; less chugging, more swirling; fewer sprightly aperitifs, more wine with seasonal food that demands a little more body and complexity. After months of saying yes to rosé, I’m choosing wine with more intention – it’s time to hunker down. I’m looking for whites that are like a good cardigan, at once coddling and breathable. I want ripeness, body and freshness, and the Atlantic-influenced wines of Galicia in northern Spain – a place that’s no stranger to wind and rain – deliver. Expressive, with a saline edge, albariño from the Rías Baixas appellation has become ubiquitous in supermarkets and rarely disappoints (try Aldi’s Specially Selected one at £8.99), neither does the fuller-bodied godello from nearby Valdeorras ( the Wine Society’s Exhibition range offers a good one for £14.95), while the blend of both those grapes and other local varieties from Galicia’s Ribeiro DO in today’s pick is a cool-climate humdinger for the colder months. Continue reading...

data.title: A good friend brings her dogs when she stays with me. I kind of dread it. What can I do? | Leading questions
data.description: People often forget social rules when dogs are involved, writes advice columnist Eleanor Gordon-Smith . But you’ll have to say something if you want things to change Read more Leading questions A good friend of mine stays with me regularly when she comes into town. She brings her husband and two dogs that don’t get along with my dog. They’ve “used the bathroom” in our house before. I try to be nice and help clean or pretend it doesn’t bother me so that they feel comfortable. But when she asks for a weekend to come back with everyone, I kind of dread it. I enjoy seeing her and she’s a great friend. I think our friendship would be better if she stayed somewhere else, but I would feel bad if she stayed in a hotel and I don’t think she’d visit as often. She cleans up after the dogs and whatnot, but I like my home to be my safe haven. This friend doesn’t handle confrontation well, but is understanding. What can I do to handle this? Eleanor says: It sounds as though you’re in the jam we all get into when we try to smooth things over: you can have the social ease of pretending something is fine; or the outcome from confessing it isn’t, but not both simultaneously. data.title: Soil in need of some TLC? Then it’s time to make room for legumes
data.description: Crops such as vetch, field beans and forage peas can improve soil if you use them as a mulch I am locked in an eternal battle with my soil. Now, I adore the earth and believe it to be miraculous in its life-giving properties. But I’d be lying if I said I don’t sometimes (or often) feel deeply frustrated with the intransigence of the heavy clay I’m working with in my veg patch. Clay soil is especially miraculous in how nutrient dense it is. Yet, those nutrients are, somewhat ironically, more challenging for gardeners to access for their crops than with other soil types. The answer – as with almost all problems faced in a chemical free, mostly no-dig garden – is adding a mulch of organic matter (either compost or well-rotted manure) that can be incorporated into the earth by insects, who will improve its texture in the process. And yet, this trusty approach is tricky in my veg patch as we live on a hill and there is about a metre’s difference between one side of the site and the other. This situation (plus the stubbornness of soil made sodden by a wet winter and then solid by a heatwave summer) has meant the layers of compost I laid over the last year have been either washed away or not particularly well incorporated into the deeper soil. Continue reading...

data.title: I spent years postponing my own joy. Here’s how I learned to say yes to the juicy bits of life | Sheree Joseph
data.description: Society tells us there is one way to live a life, and joy is a byproduct on the path there. But you don’t need a reason to enjoy the act of being alive I have been dwelling on what it means to live well. Not because I have mastered it, but because I have become very comically bad at it. I have spent years rushing through my life, panicked and convinced I was running out of time. I worried constantly about work – getting it, keeping it, doing it, caring about it too much, hating it and losing it. I obsessed over being more productive. I fretted about money, mostly about not having any left after travelling too much. I poured so much energy into dating that it’s kind of impressive I haven’t had a relationship for the last six years. But most of all I became fixated on my fertility and how it dwindled in my early 30s, leaving me to make choices most women don’t have to until later. I tried to save my eggs and couldn’t. My lack of a partner in a conservative Catholic Lebanese family became a cudgel. Continue reading...

data.title: Apostas e a palavra do Estado
data.description: O Estado brasileiro cobrou R$ 30 milhões de cada empresa autorizada a explorar apostas por cinco anos. Recebeu R$ 2,55 bilhões em 85 outorgas . Agora, a MP 1.394/2026 determina a extinção dessas autorizações em 30 dias e afasta a devolução dos valores e a indenização. A distância entre o compromisso assumido e a decisão de encerrá-lo é o centro do problema de segurança jurídica. Leia mais (10/09/2026 - 08h00)

data.title: Polisinsats vid internatskola – tre elever anhållna
data.description: Tre gymnasieelever har anhållits efter en planerad polisinsats vid internatskolan i Sigtuna i går kväll. data.title: Expert efter intrången hos finska politiker: Mycket pekar mot Ryssland
data.description: Tiotals finländska riksdagsledamöter har drabbats av inbrott. Inget har stulits och blickarna riktas österut. På torsdagen kallades ledamöterna till ett hemligt möte. – Vi kommer inte att få något rykande vapen som visar att Putin själv beordrade operationen. Men vi har ganska starka skäl att anta att Ryssland ligger bakom, säger säkerhetsexperten Henri Vanhanen.

data.title: Russell Brands rättegång börjar – stämmer historierna från 00-talet?
data.description: I början av 00-talet var Russell Brand en av Storbritanniens mest uppmärksammade komiker och programledare. Han blev känd för sin extrema persona, grova sexistiska skämt och hur han öppet "raggade" på kvinnor i tv. På senare år har regelrätta polisanmälningar gällande flera fall av våldtäkt och sexuella övergrepp gjorts mot komikern. Anklagelser Russell Brand nekar till. Nu ska en domstol avgöra om det som länge var en del av Russell Brands offentliga persona också döljer brott som han kan dömas för.

data.title: Szkoły na Mazowszu nie prowadzą stacjonarnych lekcji. Nieoficjalnie: dotyczy to 49 placówek
data.description: W piątek na Mazowszu 49 szkół odwołało stacjonarne zajęcia. Część z nich zostało zamkniętych, a w części przeniesiono uczniów na lekcje zdalne – dowiedziała się nieoficjalnie „Rzeczpospolita” ze źródeł zbliżonych do kuratorium oświaty. To reakcja na brutalne ataki w placówkach w Ostrołęce i pod Wyszkowem oraz internetowe groźby kolejnych napaści.

data.title: Piotr Zaremba: Dwie wersje „Lalki” wywołały burzę, jakiej dawno nie było
data.description: Mamy starcie dwóch filmowych adaptacji „Lalki” Bolesława Prusa. „Lalkę” jako serial Netfliksa wyreżyserował Paweł Maślona. „Lalka” kinowa, która początkowo miała być serialem TVP, to dzieło Macieja Kawalskiego. Jedni powtarzają, że ich różnorodność to wartość dla polskiej kultury. Inni opowiadają się po stronie jednej lub drugiej wersji. To burza, jakiej dawno nie było.

data.title: Lístky nepřišly, nebo jste je zapomněli doma? Volit můžete i tak
data.description: Obce musely obálky s hlasovacími lístky pro probíhající komunální a senátní volby do schránek dodat už před třemi dny. Co ale dělat v případě, že nedorazily nebo třeba omylem skončily v kontejneru s tříděným odpadem? I s touto komplikací se počítá a občané mohou k hlasování 9. nebo 10. října 2026 bez omezení.

data.title: Koťata z útulku si užila výlet do akvária. Některá zírala na ryby, jiná usnula
data.description: Zhruba dvě desítky osiřelých koťat z minnesotského útulku vyrazily na neobvyklý výlet do akvária. Zblízka pozorovaly ryby, žraloky i mořské želvy. Exkurze se koná už šestým rokem a koťatům pomáhá se socializací před odchodem do nových domovů.

data.title: Nobelovu cenu míru obdržela bývalá komisařka OSN pro lidská práva Pillayová
data.description: Norský Nobelův výbor udělil Nobelovu cenu míru za rok 2026 Navanethem „Navi“ Pillayové za její úsilí o prosazování míru a mezinárodního práva. Jihoafrickou právničku tamilského původu, která dříve působila jako soudkyně Mezinárodního trestního soudu (2003–2008) a Vysoká komisařka OSN pro lidská práva (2008–2014), výbor vybral z 287 kandidátů.

data.title: Muž pobodal soka v lásce, verze o sebeobraně nepomohla. Soud mu uložil 12 let
data.description: Silně opilý se letos v lednu v Karviné rozhodl řešit vztahové nesnáze, jenže jeho řádění málem skončilo smrtí soka v lásce, kterého pobodal. Krajský soud v Ostravě nyní poslal Karla Marša z Karviné za pokus o vraždu na dvanáct let do vězení.

data.title: Řidič ve velké rychlosti probořil ohradu, prkna prošpikovala kabinu auta
data.description: Velké štěstí měl řidič na Prachaticku, který nezvládl řízení a vyjel ze silnice, kde pobořil plot. Několik prken mu doslova prošpikovalo vůz, ale on vyvázl bez vážných zranění. Škoda na ohradě a autě je celkem 300 tisíc korun.

data.title: Vážná nehoda na Pavlově dovolené v Maroku. Jeho blízký přítel se těžce zranil
data.description: Soukromou cestu prezidenta Petra Pavla do Maroka, kvůli které se nezúčastní komunálních voleb, zkomplikovala vážná nehoda. Při havárii buginy v poušti se zranil jeho blízký přítel a spoluzakladatel herního studia SCS Software Petr Šebor. Prezident vyvázl bez zranění, členové jeho týmu pomáhali zraněným s první pomocí. Uvedl to server Aktuálně.cz s odkazem na své zdroje.

data.title: Cestujících ve vlacích přibylo o 5,2 milionu. Nákladní přeprava poklesla
data.description: Vlaky za první pololetí přepravily 96,97 milionu cestujících, meziročně o 5,21 milionu více. První i druhé čtvrtletí zaznamenaly meziroční nárůst o 2,6 milionu cestujících. Průměrná přepravní vzdálenost byla 55,67 kilometru, loni byla ve stejném období o necelý kilometr kratší. Vyplývá to z předběžných statistik zveřejněných ministerstvem dopravy.

data.title: Marhoul natočil v Hollywoodu stalinské drama Doznání. Do Česka dorazí v lednu
data.description: Hollywoodské hvězdy Rob Lowe, James Franco, Nick Nolte a Jennifer Jason Leighová hrají v komorním dramatu Doznání, jež ve Spojených státech natočil Václav Marhoul. Světovou premiéru má 15. října v soutěži festivalu ve Varšavě, poté zamíří do světové distribuce. Do českých kin přijde 28. ledna 2027.

data.title: Newyorský mrakodrap Chrysler Building čeká rekonstrukce. Projde jí i slavná špička
data.description: Jednu z nejvýraznějších dominant Manhattanu, mrakodrap Chrysler Building, čeká rozsáhlá rekonstrukce v souvislosti s jeho převzetím do dlouhodobého pronájmu. Mrakodrap ve stylu Art Deco, který se tyčí do výšky 319 metrů a má 77 podlaží, byl po svém dokončení před 96 lety nejvyšší budovou světa, než jej po necelém roce překonal nedaleký Empire State Building. Nyní Chrysler Building čeká obnova fasády i sedmiobloukové ocelové špičky s trojúhelníkovými okny.

data.title: Rychlík narazil do heveru v kolejišti, 160 lidí vezly autobusy zpět na nádraží
data.description: Nepříjemnost zažila na své cestě více než půldruhá stovka lidí, kteří dopoledne jeli vlakem přes Olomouc směrem na Prahu. Kousek od hlavního nádraží na okraji města totiž souprava narazila do části zvedáku, čímž její jízda skončila.

data.title: Státy EU schválily brzdu pro růst cen povolenek. ETS 2 se spustí v roce 2028
data.description: Členské státy EU v pátek finálně schválily úpravu emisního systému ETS 2 s cílem kontrolovat ceny chystaných povolenek pro silniční dopravu a budovy. Nová pravidla zavádějí cenovou hranici 45 eur (1100 korun) za tunu CO₂, po jejímž dosažení se do oběhu začnou automaticky uvolňovat povolenky z rezervy tržní stability (MSR).

data.title: V Polsku po útocích na školách zadrželi přes deset lidí, teenageři hrozili smrtí
data.description: Polská policie zadržela přes deset lidí, kteří na internetu vyhrožovali, že někoho zabijí nebo zveřejnili fotografie nožů. Mezi zadrženými jsou hlavně dospívající chlapci. V polských školách platí zpřísněná bezpečnostní opatření, protože na dvou z nich v předchozích dnech mladíci zaútočili nožem. Jedna žena zemřela, více než deset dalších utrpělo zranění.

data.title: Vystrašený srnec se vřítil do budovy školy, studentka mu ještě podržela dveře
data.description: Velmi neobvyklou návštěvu měli ve středu na gymnáziu v Uherském Hradišti. Do budovy u nejrušnější ulice v centru města vběhl vystrašený srnec, jedna ze studentek mu dokonce podržela otevřené vstupní dveře do budovy. Přivolaní myslivci museli zvíře vyvléct ven a vypustili ho k blízké řece.

data.title: Na kandidátkách je 858 Nováků. V Měrovicích se volí skoro jen mezi příbuznými
data.description: Už jen složení jmen na všech 22 555 kandidátkách ve více než 6 000 obcích v celém Česku dává jasně vědět, že nadcházející komunální volby jsou poměrně věrným zrcadlem celé populace. data.title: Starosta v Náchodě roky vyhrává, ale jiní chtějí posílit. I ostrou kampaní
data.description: Na dramatické překreslení politické mapy Náchoda to nejspíš nevypadá. Starosta Jan Birke tu vládne se značnou převahou téměř šestnáct let a chce pokračovat. Kromě jeho uskupení jde do voleb pět dalších subjektů, což kopíruje situaci v zastupitelstvu. Při minulých volbách kandidovalo devět uskupení, ale dvě propadla.

data.title: Malý chlapec se v noci vzbudil a vydal se hledat matku. Ta zatím popíjela v parku
data.description: Běžně v tu dobu už takto malé děti spí. V noci na čtvrtek krátce po 23. hodině však zhruba sedmiletý chlapec stál sám poblíž autobusové zastávky v Brně a plakal. Jak se ukázalo, byl nešťastný z toho, že doma nemohl najít svou matku, když se vzbudil, a vydal se ji hledat.

data.title: Labouristé v Londýně obhájili Starmerův mandát, šéf zelených pohořel
data.description: Labouristická strana aktuálního britského premiéra Andyho Burnhama zvítězila ve čtvrtečních doplňovacích volbách do Dolní sněmovny v londýnském obvodu Holborn a St Pancras. Labouristé křeslo, které uvolnil někdejší premiér Keir Starmer, obhájili proti silné výzvě levicových zelených. To by mělo přispět k politickému posílení současného předsedy vlády Burnhama.

data.title: Europoslanci odmítli legitimitu ruské Dumy. Zastali se jí Slováci i několik Čechů
data.description: Když se v Evropském parlamentu hlasovalo, zda bude Brusel považovat volby do ruské Státní dumy za nelegitimní, objevilo se mezi poslanci i několik zastánců Ruska. Proti rezoluci hlasovali mimo jiné Češi Ondřej Dostál, Kateřina Konečná a Ivan David či Slováci Luboš Blaha a Milan Mazurek.

data.title: Nobelova cena 2026: přehled vítězů a termíny vyhlášení dalších laureátů
data.description: Nejvyšším vyznamenáním na poli vědy a techniky, stejně jako v oblasti zásluh o rozvoj lidstva, je Nobelova cena udělovaná v celkem šesti kategoriích. Laureáty, jež vždy v říjnu vyhlašuje několik švédských a norských institucí, se vyjma věhlasu mohou těšit i na medaili, diplom a milionovou odměnu. Slavnostní předání ocenění každoročně připadá na prosinec.

data.title: Macinka vyrazil do Černoučku. Zjišťoval, co místní říkají na prezidentovu dovolenou
data.description: Ministr zahraničí Petr Macinka (Motoristé) se ve čtvrtek vydal do Černoučku na Litoměřicku, kde má trvalé bydliště prezident Petr Pavel. Ten se kvůli soukromé cestě do Maroka nezúčastní komunálních voleb, které v pátek začínají. Macinka se v obci zastavil v místní hospodě a zajímal se o názory prezidentových sousedů. „Po diskusi v délce dvou malých piv raději neříkám nic,“ napsal na Facebooku.

data.title: Česká superstřela čeká na bojový křest. Armáda by měla zájem, říká mluvčí zbrojovky
data.description: Český obranný průmysl slaví výjimečný úspěch. Zbrojovka LPP Holding vyvinula první stoprocentně českou střelu s plochou dráhou letu Narwhal, se kterou nedávno ovládla prestižní technologickou soutěž NATO. „Nyní systém dotestováváme a plánujeme jeho ověření na bojišti v nejbližších měsících. Od toho se pak odvine sériová výroba,“ říká v rozhovoru pro iDNES.cz Martina Tauberová, ředitelka pro vnější vztahy skupiny LPP Holding.

data.title: Ruské úřady hrozí tresty za zprávy o moru. Bezpečnostní opatření odvolaly
data.description: Ruský cenzurní úřad Roskomnadzor pohrozil médiím postihem za šíření nepravdivých zpráv o výskytu moru na Sibiři. data.title: Havlíček: Do Střední Asie vyvážíme zboží, ne lidská práva. Teď míříme na Ukrajinu
data.description: Ekonomická diplomacie je tvrdý byznys, v němž rozhodují kvalitní výrobky, financování a kontakty s politickými špičkami. Ministr průmyslu Karel Havlíček to zdůraznil v debatě iDNES Lounge, která se uskutečnila v Brně na Mezinárodním strojírenském veletrhu. Spolu s ním debatovali také šéf EGAP David Havlíček a prezident Hospodářské komory Zdeněk Zajíček. Také na Ukrajině podle nich české firmy čeká ostrá soutěž a vděčnost jim zakázky nezajistí.

data.title: Saudi weekly consumer spending surges 23% to $4.4bn on education outlays
data.description: Saudi Arabia's consumer spending surged 23.4% to SR16.51 billion ($4.4 billion) for the week ending October 3, primarily driven by a 142.8% increase in education-related expenditures due to the new academic year. Other sectors also saw growth, with food and beverage spending up 41% and transportation by 27.8%, while spending in hotels declined by 9.8%.

data.title: Exclusive: Details of visa-free travel to Europe expected at GCC-EU summit
data.description: During the upcoming EU-GCC summit on October 24 in Riyadh, GCC Secretary-General Jasem Mohamed Al-Budaiwi announced that a significant step towards waiving Schengen visa requirements for citizens of Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Oman, Bahrain, and Kuwait is anticipated. data.title: Yemen military official: We are advancing on many fronts and Sanaa is the main battle
data.description: Yemeni Deputy Minister of Defense, Major General Samir Al-Sabri, reported significant military progress in the Battle of Marib, highlighting that Sanaa is the main focus of the current conflict. He indicated that multiple fronts, including the West Coast and Taiz Governorate, are actively engaged, with ongoing battles and strategic control of key locations like Bab al-Mandab and Al-Waziyah essential to countering Houthi forces. Al-Sabri emphasized the importance of disrupting Houthi supply lines and acknowledged the role of international support in the conflict.

data.title: Book Review: ‘The Anthropocene Reviewed’
data.description: John Green’s “The Anthropocene Reviewed,” from 2021, is a book of 44 brief essays. It takes the star ratings familiar from online reviews and applies them to the marvels and oddities of a world shaped by people. Most of the essays grew out of the author’s well-liked podcast of the same name, reworked and expanded for print. Each one rates a topic from one to five stars, playing on internet review culture. Canada geese, Diet Dr Pepper, and the QWERTY keyboard are among the subjects. Anthropocene

data.title: Settlers damage olive trees in West Bank’s Salfit district
data.description: Israeli forces on Thursday closed agricultural roads in the western area of Deir Ballut, in the central West Bank district of Salfit, while settlers attacked agricultural land in the nearby town of Kafr Al-Dik. Local sources said that Israeli bulldozers blocked several agricultural roads in western Deir Ballut with earth barriers, preventing farmers from reaching their lands. In Kafr Al-Dik, settlers attacked agricultural land owned by farmer Ali Abdullah Qassem in the northern part of the town.

data.title: Enseignants : une journée de célébration, peu de raisons de se réjouir
data.description: Au moment où le monde célèbre la Journée mondiale des enseignants pour sa 60e fois le 5 octobre 2026, ceux du Burundi restent confrontés à des conditions de travail difficiles. Enseignants insuffisants, faibles salaires, manque de matériel didactique et classes surchargées figurent parmi leurs principales préoccupations. Les syndicats appellent à la révision de la grille salariale de 2016 afin de l’adapter au coût actuel de la vie.

data.title: Primus Ligue, 6e journée — Le championnat se déploie
data.description: On croyait le championnat attaché à une seule enceinte, il se révèle capable de régner partout. Faute d'Urukundo, impraticable en semaine hormis le dimanche, la commission d'organisation a choisi de ne rien annuler et de tout réinventer. Dans sa circulaire FFB/COC/065/2026 parue ce 7 octobre à Bujumbura, la Fédération ne parle pas de contrainte. Elle organise la résilience. La 6e journée de Primus Ligue ne se disloque pas, elle se déploie.

data.title: Classement du 7 octobre 2026 : le Burundi gagne deux places parmi les 211 nations affiliées à la FIFA
data.description:
Il y a des chiffres qui ne disent rien. Et il y en a d'autres qui racontent une histoire. 
 Ce 7 octobre 2026 , la FIFA a, comme à son habitude, égrené son chapelet mondial sur les 211 nations qui lui sont "sectatrices". Un classement froid, presque clinique, qui s'étend de l'Espagne, reine incontestée trônant au sommet du monde, jusqu'aux plus modestes confins du football.

data.title: De nouvelles infrastructures communautaires inaugurées à Kanyabayonga grâce à un financement de la MONUSCO
data.description: La cité de Kanyabayonga, située à cheval entre les territoires de Lubero et de Rutshuru, dispose désormais d’un marché de fruits, d’un moulin communautaire ainsi que d’un système d’éclairage public. data.title: Equateur : une mère et ses deux enfants tués par un hippopotame à Bikoro
data.description: Une tragédie a frappé la communauté riveraine du lac Ntumba dans la nuit de mercredi 7 à jeudi 8 octobre 2026. Une mère de famille et ses deux enfants ont été mortellement attaqués par un hippopotame au village Ikoko Bonginda, dans le territoire de Bikoro  (Équateur). Selon l'organisation non gouvernementale de défense des droits humains « Cadre pour le Développement et le Bien-être » (CADEB), cet incident tragique s'inscrit dans une série noire d'affrontements répétés entre les habitants et la faune sauvage.

data.title: Grand Kasaï : la planification stratégique à l’horizon 2050 au cœur du Forum de Mbuji-Mayi
data.description: La mise en place d'une planification régionale à l'horizon 2050, l'accélération de l'électrification ainsi que le désenclavement des infrastructures constituent les piliers des quatorze recommandations adoptées lors du Forum sur le développement du Grand Kasaï qui se clôture ce vendredi 9 octobre à Mbuji-Mayi. Organisées par le diocèse catholique de Mbuji-mayi, ces assises de trois jours ont réuni des délégués venus de différentes provinces de la République démocratique du Congo et de l'étranger.

data.title: Les détenus de la prison centrale du Cinquantenaire au Kwilu privés de nourriture depuis cinq jours
data.description: Les détenus de la prison centrale du Cinquantenaire, dans la province du Kwilu, seraient privés de nourriture depuis cinq jours, selon les affirmations de la société civile locale ce jeudi 8 octobre. data.title: Haut-Lomami : six morts dans un conflit coutumier à Butumba
data.description: Un conflit coutumier a tourné au drame dans la chefferie de Butumba, territoire de Bukama, dans la province du Haut-Lomami. Six personnes ont été tuées mardi 6 octobre, dont certaines incendiées, dans des affrontements entre des partisans de leaders qui se disputent le pouvoir après la mort du dernier chef. Sept personnes ont également été grièvement blessées, rapporte ce jeudi 8 octobre l’administrateur du territoire de Bukama.

data.title: Faux : Le BC Génération Espoir de Lubumbashi  n’est pas bloqué à Kinshasa faute de moyen
data.description: Des informations relayées sur les réseaux sociaux font état d’un prétendu blocage de l’équipe du BC Génération Espoir de Lubumbashi à Kinshasa en raison de difficultés financières. Contacté par Radio Okapi, le président du club, Daddhy Yuma, dément ces allégations et affirme que l’équipe n’a pas été abandonnée dans la capitale. Selon lui, plusieurs joueurs ont déjà regagné Lubumbashi, tandis que d’autres ont choisi de rester à Kinshasa de leur propre gré.

data.title: Aucun centre de traitement d'Ebola n'a fermé ses portes à Beni
data.description: Le coordinateur de la riposte contre la maladie à virus Ebola à Beni, au Nord-Kivu, a démenti, ce jeudi 8 octobre 2026, les rumeurs circulant sur les réseaux sociaux faisant état de la fermeture des centres de traitement dans la région. Les rumeurs virales faisant état d'un arrêt des activités dans plusieurs structures de prise en charge ont contraint la direction médicale de la riposte à intervenir publiquement pour rassurer la population.

data.title: Chapeando: La incoherencia y su revés (+ Podcast)
data.description: Son muchos los que lloran por la familia que dejaron en Cuba, que presumen de nostalgia de la Isla en sus post en Facebook y al mismo tiempo piden a Trump que bombardee La Habana ya. En realidad usan a la familia -que les importa un bledo- con el mismo fin pero desde otra dimensión: se trata de denigrar y acusar al gobierno cubano como violador de los derechos humanos, lo cual sirve al mismo propósito: justificar cualquier tipo de agresión contra Cuba, incluida la militar. He ahí la coherencia de su incoherencia. The post Chapeando: La incoherencia y su revés (+ Podcast) first appeared on Cubadebate .

data.title: Crecida del río Ulúa provoca filtraciones en zonas bajas de El Progreso
data.description: El Progreso, Yoro. La Comisión Permanente de Contingencias (Copeco) mantiene este jueves vigilancia ante la crecida del río Ulúa , especialmente en las zonas bajas del Valle de Sula, donde ya se reportan filtraciones de agua y una ruptura de bordo en uno de los sectores. Personal de la Regional II de Copeco realiza recorridos desde Pimienta hasta diferentes puntos del Valle de Sula para supervisar las condiciones del río y mantener informada a la población ante posibles afectaciones. Alberto López, meteorólogo de Copeco, informó que el nivel del río Ulúa aumentó en las últimas horas y pasó de dos metros a 3.80 metros en la estación hidrometeorológica ubicada en el Puente de la Democracia, en El Progreso, Yoro. “Las mediciones que nos arroja el sistema de vigilancia pasó de tener dos metros de nivel el río Ulúa a 3.80, aumentó 1 metro con 80 centímetros”, explicó López. El funcionario indicó que, debido al incremento del caudal , se reportaron las primeras filtraciones en la colonia Policarpo Paz García. Además, Copeco recibió información sobre una pequeña ruptura de bordo en los sectores de San José del Cayo y Miller. López señaló que un equipo de Copeco fue enviado para verificar las condiciones en esas comunidades y realizar las evaluaciones correspondientes. La información también fue trasladada al Centro de Operaciones Regional de San Pedro Sula para las acciones correspondientes. De acuerdo con el funcionario, en San José del Cayo ya se reportan inundaciones y no solamente filtraciones. Según los reportes recibidos por Copeco, la ruptura del bordo habría provocado acumulación de agua en la calle principal del sector. En cuanto al nivel del río, López explicó que la estación Puente de la Democracia registra actualmente 3.80 metros y mantiene un nivel de alerta verde . Sin embargo, la gráfica de monitoreo muestra una tendencia al alza. El meteorólogo señaló que el nuevo sistema de vigilancia permite monitorear en tiempo real el comportamiento del río y generar alertas con anticipación ante posibles inundaciones en el Valle de Sula. “Podemos avisar con 19 horas de antelación que viene una inundación para el Valle de Sula”, afirmó López al explicar el funcionamiento del sistema de monitoreo. El funcionario indicó que, ante la ruptura de bordo reportada, existe riesgo de afectaciones en las zonas bajas de El Progreso. No obstante, aclaró que el comportamiento del río podría presentar aumentos y descensos en su nivel. “Lo que yo le puedo mencionar es que vamos a tener picos de subida y picos de bajada en cuanto al nivel y va a estar haciendo afectaciones e incidencias en las partes bajas”, explicó.

data.title: Más de 270 puntos de control y 550 licencias decomisadas en el Feriado Morazánico
data.description: San Pedro Sula, Cortés . La Policía Nacional ha desplegado más de 270 puntos de control en la zona noroccidental de Honduras durante el Feriado Morazánico , como parte de los operativos para reforzar la seguridad vial y prevenir accidentes de tránsito. El subinspector Luis Soto , de la Dirección Nacional de Vialidad y Transporte (DNVT), explicó que los controles se desarrollan en coordinación con agentes de la Dirección Nacional de Prevención y Seguridad Comunitaria (DNPSC). Soto detalló que los operativos están dirigidos principalmente a garantizar la seguridad de los hondureños que durante este período de vacaciones se desplazan hacia sus lugares de origen o destinos turísticos de la zona noroccidental. Como parte de las acciones preventivas, los agentes realizan pruebas de alcoholemia y antidoping a los conductores en diferentes puntos de control. Según Soto, estos procedimientos buscan evitar accidentes y otras tragedias en las carreteras. El subinspector también informó que, desde el inicio del Feriado Morazánico, la Policía ha decomisado más de 550 permisos de conducir a personas que han cometido infracciones a la Ley de Tránsito. “Son estos conductores que por una u otra falta a la ley de tránsito han caído en estas infracciones y se ha hecho el cumplimiento a la normativa de la ley”, explicó Soto. El despliegue policial también incluye más de 100 patrullas de carretera distribuidas en los departamentos que conforman la zona noroccidental del país, según detalló el funcionario. Además de las labores de control, los agentes brindan asistencia a conductores que presentan desperfectos o quedan varados en las carreteras durante sus desplazamientos. Soto hizo un llamado a los conductores a mantener la prudencia al volante y respetar las normas de tránsito durante el feriado. Entre las principales recomendaciones está evitar el uso del teléfono celular mientras se conduce, utilizar el cinturón de seguridad y no manejar bajo los efectos del alcohol u otras sustancias. Las autoridades mantienen los operativos durante el Feriado Morazánico con el objetivo de prevenir accidentes y garantizar la seguridad de las personas que se movilizan por las carreteras del país.

data.title: Hondureño es sentenciado por introducir ilegalmente a 188 inmigrantes a EEUU
data.description: Houston, Estados Unidos. Un hondureño de 35 años fue sentenciado a seis años de prisión federal en Estados Unidos por su participación en una red dedicada al traslado ilegal de migrantes hacia ese país, informó el Departamento de Justicia. El condenado fue identificado como Eliseo Henríquez Joya, conocido con el alias de "Cheyo", quien residía de manera irregular en Houston y, según las autoridades, dirigía una organización que habría participado en el ingreso clandestino de cerca de 200 personas a territorio estadounidense. La red utilizaba camiones de carga, vehículos refrigerados y tráileres para movilizar a los migrantes. Algunos de estos automotores habían sido modificados con espacios ocultos y paredes falsas en las áreas destinadas a transportar mercancías, con el objetivo de esconder a grupos numerosos de personas. Las condiciones en las que eran trasladados representaban un grave riesgo. De acuerdo con el Departamento de Justicia , los compartimentos permanecían completamente cerrados, sin ventilación ni aire acondicionado y sin una salida disponible para quienes permanecían dentro. El juez federal David Morales se refirió a las condiciones del traslado durante el proceso y consideró que "es un milagro que nadie hubiera muerto" debido al peligro al que fueron expuestos los migrantes. La participación de Henríquez Joya en la operación fue establecida, entre otras evidencias, mediante información recuperada de teléfonos celulares. Los investigadores utilizaron esas pruebas para relacionarlo con los movimientos de la organización. Según el expediente, "Cheyo" tenía un papel central en la logística de los viajes. Se encargaba de buscar a los conductores y coordinaba los traslados, además de indicarles cuántas personas debían transportar y los puntos donde debían recogerlas y dejarlas.
