data.title: Only 40% of Romanians have a financial plan for next 12 months, study says
data.description: Only 40% of Romanians have a financial plan for the next 12 months, according to the first national study evaluating the impact of a financial education program. The study was launched by Banometru, a free financial education program developed by the Education for Real Life Association (AEVR) with the support of ING Bank Romania. One of the study’s most important findings related to financial planning, one of the key indicators of financial health. Among the general population, only 40% of respondents said they have a financial plan for the next 12 months. Only 43% of Romanians follow a budget at least to some extent. At the same time, 56% of them say they have money left over at the end of the month. Finally, only 42% of Romanians save for long-term goals. The data showed that preparing for unexpected expenses and building a financial reserve continue to pose significant challenges. The results suggested that financial education helps people link today’s decisions to their long- term goals: managing their expenses and saving regularly, maintaining financial stability from month to month, and, over time, building an emergency fund or a financial retirement plan. People who have a better understanding of money take steps to increase their income. Launched in 2016 to support people facing financial difficulties and debt-related problems, Banometru has evolved into a comprehensive financial wellness program that combines one- on-one coaching sessions, financial education, practical tools, and community support. Over its 10 years of operation, Banometru has reached approximately 350,000 participants, provided 15,569 hours of financial coaching, and served as the first exposure to financial education for 70% of its beneficiaries. Between 2021 and 2026, participants reported mobilizing over RON 8.18 million: RON 3.86 million in repaid debt, RON 2.49 million in savings, and RON 1.84 million in additional income. “Simply reading or hearing about what you should do is, unfortunately, not enough. For us, the most important conclusion is that change happens when you respect each person’s pace and their own idea of what’s best for them. Change is seen in everyday actions,” said Corneliu Ionescu, president and founder of AEVR and the initiator of Banometru. The study “Banometer—10 Years. In Your Financial Shoes” was conducted by Claudia Petrescu, Research Scientist at the Institute for Quality of Life Research of the Romanian Academy, and Raluca Șandru, a professor at the Faculty of Business at Babeș-Bolyai University, with contributions from Silvia Mișu, Director of Development and Innovation at AEVR. The study uses OECD/INFE indicators and methodological benchmarks and compares three groups: individuals who participated in the Banometru program at least 12 months before the survey, individuals entering the program before accessing its services, and a comparison group from the general population, representative by gender, age group, and region, composed of individuals who have not participated in financial education programs.

data.title: Romania’s insolvencies rise 12% to highest level since 2018, large company cases more than double
data.description: More than 5,250 companies in Romania became insolvent in the first nine months of 2026, approximately 12% more than in the same period last year, marking the highest level since 2018, according to an analysis by CITR based on estimates from the National Trade Register Office (ONRC). During the same period, the number of companies with assets worth more than EUR 1 million that entered insolvency proceedings increased by 65%, while the number of those with assets worth more than EUR 4 million more than doubled (marking a 141% increase in proceedings in this category). “A large company is effectively financed by its suppliers, and when it stops making payments, the difficulties spread along the chain. The warning signs are already visible in the data: declining margins, rising debt, overdue payments to suppliers concentrated among undercapitalized companies, while agriculture is simultaneously showing pressure on balance sheets, in banks, and in courts. For companies that are still viable, the timing of intervention determines how much can still be saved,” said Paul-Dieter Cîrlănaru, CEO of CITR. Out of the nearly 230 additional insolvencies compared with last year, more than 190 came from just two sectors: agriculture (+94) and construction (+97). At the same time, trade and manufacturing recorded slight decreases in insolvency proceedings (approximately 5% in trade and approximately 6% in manufacturing). The highest number of insolvencies was recorded in agriculture (+52.5%), with more than 90 additional proceedings compared with the same period last year. As a result, agriculture has become the second least profitable sector of the economy, while the non-performing loan rate rose from 2.7% in October 2024 to 9.8% in March 2026. Construction is also affected, recording an increase in insolvencies of more than 10% and exceeding the threshold of 1,000 companies in insolvency in the first three quarters. Regionally, the North-East was the region with the fastest growth in insolvencies (+21.8%) in the first three quarters of the year. Vaslui doubled its number of proceedings, Bacău recorded an increase of 48.5%, and Suceava one of 42.1%. Significant increases were also recorded in Bistrița-Năsăud (+77.6%), Vrancea (+69.0%), Arad (+41.2%), Brașov (+37.8%), and Hunedoara (+30.8%). At the opposite end, the North-West is the only region where the number of insolvencies decreased (–5.7%), with declines in Cluj (–15.2%), Bihor (–11.9%), and Sălaj (–41.4%). Constanța also recorded a decrease of 15.1%. Bucharest remains the main center of insolvencies, with more than 860 cases, accounting for 18% of the total, but recording modest growth of 4.1%. According to CITR, a large company entering insolvency does not remain an isolated case. International economic research on trade credit chains shows that when a customer becomes insolvent, its suppliers suffer losses, and their own insolvency risk increases in line with the size of the loss. The effect is stronger during periods of economic slowdown and among suppliers with limited capital and liquidity. The same studies show that the chain of non-payments usually stops at large, liquid companies with access to financing, which absorb the shocks. When these very companies enter insolvency, the buffer disappears. "In Romania, the conditions for contagion are present: supplier credit is a major source of financing, undercapitalized companies account for more than a third of trade payment arrears, and the value of payment defaults is increasing. For this reason, the doubling of insolvencies among large companies is a warning sign that goes beyond the actual number of recorded cases," CITR said in a press release.

data.title: OAR Bucharest: Romania’s architectural design market grows tenfold in 25 years
data.description: Romania’s architectural design market has expanded from less than EUR 30 million in 2001 to more than EUR 300 million in 2026, according to estimates from the Bucharest branch of the Romanian Order of Architects (OAR). The capital city accounts for approximately half of the national market. The figures were released on Thursday, October 8, as OAR Bucharest marked 25 years since the professional organisation was established. The Bucharest branch has grown from 1,290 members in 2001 to 4,788 active architects today, representing approximately one-third of the country’s architects. Women now form the majority, with 2,601 female and 2,187 male members, compared with 480 women and 810 men at the organisation’s launch. An estimated 3,500 to 4,000 architecture firms operate across Romania, according to the same report. While architecture businesses rarely exceeded EUR 1 million in annual turnover in 2001, the largest firms now generate EUR 3-6 million, while the top ten have combined revenues of EUR 20-30 million. Average design fees have also increased from EUR 3-10 per sqm to EUR 15-45 per sqm. OAR Bucharest attributed part of the rise to more detailed projects and larger multidisciplinary teams that now include BIM managers, nearly zero-energy building auditors, and specialists in traffic, landscape, acoustics, and environmental certification. “Artificial intelligence, BIM, decarbonisation, climate change, and the industrialisation of construction are not topics for conferences in 2030,” said OAR Bucharest president Sergiu Petrea. “They are already affecting our profession today.” The organisation is working with foresight specialist Bülent Duagi on scenarios examining how architecture could evolve by 2051. The exercise considers different levels of AI involvement in design and regulatory compliance, alongside climate and seismic pressures ranging from gradual change to overlapping shocks such as extreme heat, floods, and a major earthquake. “The question is no longer whether the profession will change, because it is changing already,” Sergiu Petrea said. “The question is whether we will shape that change or merely watch it happen.” Initial consultations with members identified three priorities: making architectural practice more sustainable, clarifying the architect’s value as AI automates tasks, and strengthening trust and cooperation within the profession. OAR branches in Bucharest, Iași, Timiș, and Transylvania are also signing the BITT strategic partnership. The agreement is intended to simplify professional processes, support joint initiatives, and create a shared database of tools, resources, and best practices. The Romanian Order of Architects is a public-interest organisation established under Law 184/2001 to regulate the profession, protect the title of architect, and promote architectural quality.

While architecture businesses rarely exceeded EUR 1 million in annual turnover in 2001, the largest firms now generate EUR 3-6 million, while the top ten have combined revenues of EUR 20-30 million. Average design fees have also increased from EUR 3-10 per sqm to EUR 15-45 per sqm. OAR Bucharest attributed part of the rise to more detailed projects and larger multidisciplinary teams that now include BIM managers, nearly zero-energy building auditors, and specialists in traffic, landscape, acoustics, and environmental certification. “Artificial intelligence, BIM, decarbonisation, climate change, and the industrialisation of construction are not topics for conferences in 2030,” said OAR Bucharest president Sergiu Petrea. “They are already affecting our profession today.” The organisation is working with foresight specialist Bülent Duagi on scenarios examining how architecture could evolve by 2051. The exercise considers different levels of AI involvement in design and regulatory compliance, alongside climate and seismic pressures ranging from gradual change to overlapping shocks such as extreme heat, floods, and a major earthquake. “The question is no longer whether the profession will change, because it is changing already,” Sergiu Petrea said. “The question is whether we will shape that change or merely watch it happen.” Initial consultations with members identified three priorities: making architectural practice more sustainable, clarifying the architect’s value as AI automates tasks, and strengthening trust and cooperation within the profession. OAR branches in Bucharest, Iași, Timiș, and Transylvania are also signing the BITT strategic partnership. The agreement is intended to simplify professional processes, support joint initiatives, and create a shared database of tools, resources, and best practices. The Romanian Order of Architects is a public-interest organisation established under Law 184/2001 to regulate the profession, protect the title of architect, and promote architectural quality.

data.title: TikTok risks fine worth 6% of global turnover after 2024 Romania election interference, European Commission says
data.description: The European Commission has opened an investigation into Chinese social media platform TikTok under the Digital Services Act (DSA) after the 2024 Romanian elections. The investigation could result in fines of up to 6% of TikTok's global turnover, according to Thomas Regnier, spokesperson for the European Commission’s Directorate-General for Communication. According to the European official, after the first round of the 2024 Romanian presidential elections, when far-right surprise candidate Calin Georgescu came in first place, Romanian authorities sent the Commission classified documents. The documents showed that massive disinformation campaigns had taken place on TikTok, amplified by bots. “This is where we suddenly enter the territory of the DSA, because it holds online platforms accountable for the role they could play in elections. (...) In the meantime, we have opened an investigation against TikTok under the DSA; it risks fines of up to 6% of its global turnover, representing a considerable amount,” the spokesperson explained, cited by Agerpres . After receiving the documents from Romania, the European Commission asked TikTok for information. Regnier stressed that the Commission was not directly interested in who won the elections. “The only thing we want is to ensure that, regardless of who wins the elections, the result reflects the choice of the citizens, and only the citizens, and that no technology executive has intervened in the electoral process because of their own preferences,” Thomas Regnier said. Romania’s Constitutional Court annulled the results of the first round of the presidential election in December 2024, which had been won by independent candidate Călin Georgescu. Since then, the far-right politician has been arrested for fraud . The same month, the European Union opened formal proceedings against the social media platform TikTok over its alleged failure to limit election interference during Romania’s presidential election. On April 2, 2025, a report prepared by TikTok as a signatory to the Code of Conduct on Disinformation under the Digital Services Act presented the threats observed in connection with Romania’s November 2024 presidential election, the measures taken in the run-up to the election, and interactions with national authorities and local experts before the election, as well as with national and EU authorities after the election. In the report, TikTok documented some of the threats it had observed in connection with Romania’s presidential election, mentioning the removal of six covert influence operation (CIO) networks in 2024 that had been identified as specifically targeting an audience in Romania. The platform also noted it had removed more than 5,500 pieces of election-related content in Romania for violating its policies on disinformation, harassment, and hate speech.

data.title: DroneFlight launches Romanian BVLOS drone services with EUR 300,000 investment
data.description: DroneFlight Romania announced that it began operations with an initial investment of EUR 300,000, targeting companies that require recurring drone surveillance, inspection, and monitoring services. The capital will finance local operations, authorisations, staff training, command infrastructure, software, and the transfer of technology and procedures from the Netherlands. The company has three shareholders: Romanian entrepreneur Ștefan Ecxarcu and two Dutch partners with around ten years of experience in the drone industry. Its Romanian operation uses a model already deployed commercially in the Netherlands, adapted to local costs, regulations, and customer needs, it said. “Several years ago, I considered that the Romanian market was not sufficiently prepared,” Ecxarcu said. “We resumed the discussion last year, when we saw that the technology had matured and security companies and infrastructure operators had begun looking for such services.” BVLOS, or “beyond visual line of sight,” refers to flights in which a drone operates outside the pilot’s direct field of vision. Such operations can cover large areas along programmed routes or respond to alerts without requiring the pilot to remain close to the aircraft. DroneFlight’s Drone-as-a-Service model allows customers to use drones without buying and maintaining their own equipment or establishing internal pilot teams. Depending on the project, the company can supply drones, automated docking and charging stations, remote piloting, monitoring, maintenance, and regulatory documentation. Its initial target sectors are logistics parks and warehouses, energy and utilities, construction, industrial facilities, and private security. Services will include perimeter patrols, alert verification, incident documentation, infrastructure and photovoltaic panel inspections, construction-site monitoring, and surveillance of areas difficult to cover with personnel or fixed cameras. Most BVLOS flights fall under the “specific” category of European drone regulations and require a risk assessment and operational authorisation from the relevant aviation authority. DroneFlight said it would prepare the necessary SORA or PDRA documentation and assist customers with obtaining project-specific approvals. The company currently has four employees in technical, operational, commercial, and security roles. Over the medium term, it plans to build a Romanian remote operations centre capable of serving customers domestically and in other European markets. The European Commission estimates that Europe’s drone services market could reach EUR 14.5 billion by 2030, with average annual growth of 12.3% and approximately 145,000 direct jobs created across the EU, according to data quoted by DroneFlight. The company will formally present its services at the Romanian Security Fair, held at Romexpo in Bucharest from October 14 to 16.

data.title: Romania’s EUR 100 mln EU-funded medical appointment platform reportedly failing patients
data.description: Only around 2,500 appointments were made through the platform in its first month. Patients struggle to navigate the system and find available consultation slots, Ziarul Financiar reported. Meanwhile, Euronews Romania found that the platform displayed no available appointments for the day of its check or the following days. Family doctors reportedly do not have access to the system, while patients continue to book consultations through conventional channels and attend appointments with paper documents. Although almost 3,500 medical service providers have registered on the platform, few appear to have synchronised their schedules with it. Selecting a specific provider can make it impossible to book an appointment, according to the reports. The platform is therefore accessible but appears to offer limited practical functionality, with patients often having to rely on the usual methods of arranging consultations. The National Health Insurance House (CNAS), which operates the public health insurance system, did not respond to questions from Ziarul Financiar about the reported problems. The platform’s IT implementation was handled by Rasirom, a state-owned autonomous administration specialising in physical and IT security solutions, operating under the coordination of the Romanian Intelligence Service (SRI).

data.title: Romania’s PM-designate Luca Niculescu sees silver lining despite parties’ conflicting positions
data.description: However, the parties remain divided over the economic policy and political composition of a new government, leaving no clear path to a stable parliamentary majority. Luca Niculescu suggested that finance minister Alexandru Nazare could retain his position in the new cabinet [consistent with the consensus on the continuing fiscal consolidation], but said it was too early to discuss ministerial appointments. He also has yet to decide whether the government will comprise politicians or technocrats, an option openly rejected by the Social Democrats (PSD). “[Nazare] enjoys credibility among foreign partners; he is someone who can have his place in a government,” Niculescu told Antena 3 , adding that “this discussion is premature”. The Social Democrats and Liberals remain divided over the government formula. Speaking after consultations with the Liberals (PNL), Niculescu acknowledged that proposals previously put forward by the PSD did not have the same level of support from PNL. It remained unclear whether he was referring to economic policy or the composition of the government. The differences over economic policy are well established, hardly conciliable, and contributed to the collapse of the four-party centrist coalition. Reconciling the parties’ positions may therefore require a government with limited room for manoeuvre, focused on day-to-day administration and meeting fiscal commitments rather than implementing meaningful reforms – something like the current government of PM Ilie Bolojan but with Luca Niculescu and with full [but only formal] power. PSD wants a political government, but refuses to govern alone. PSD leader Sorin Grindeanu expressed a clear preference for a government composed of politicians rather than technocrats, but ruled out a PSD-only cabinet. Although PNL and the Hungarian party UDMR had signalled that they could support such a cabinet in Parliament, Grindeanu argued that this would leave the Social Democrats carrying the political burden of governing without adequate support. He called on PNL and UDMR to join a future government as [junior] partners. Otherwise, he said, PSD would be prepared to support a minority PNL-UDMR cabinet from outside the government, according to an interview with Antena 3 . The position is notable given that PSD, together with the far-right AUR, backed the May 5 no-confidence motion against the government led by Ilie Bolojan, which also included PNL, UDMR, and the reformist Save Romania Union (USR). PNL, meanwhile, reaffirmed that it would no longer join a governing coalition with PSD following the motion. However, it signalled that it could initially vote in favour of a minority PSD cabinet while remaining in opposition. Grindeanu subsequently rejected that option. PNL also said it would support Niculescu’s government in the parliamentary investiture vote regardless of its composition, without taking part in the cabinet. “I informed Mr Luca Niculescu that PNL does not intend to participate in this government,” PNL leader Ilie Bolojan said. At that moment, however, he was unaware of PSD's proposal to support a PNL-UDMR minority cabinet, and he assumed PSD would be part of the government. He explained that the party had decided against joining any government with PSD in the current political context. If the Social Democrats enter the next government, PNL will move into opposition. UDMR also signalled its willingness to support the investiture of a new government without necessarily joining it. Antal Árpád, the mayor of Sfântu Gheorghe, said the party would wait for the positions of PSD and PNL before deciding whether to participate in the cabinet, according to Mediafax . UDMR’s only red line, he added, was cooperation with parties in the sovereignist camp. PSD turns down invitation to form a minority government. Later, Grindeanu explicitly rejected the idea of a minority PSD government, saying it would put the party in a vulnerable position. Instead, he said PSD would vote in favour of a minority PNL-UDMR cabinet. In response, USR MP Cătălin Drulă noted that PNL, UDMR, and USR had already proposed a minority government led by Siegfried Mureșan, an option that PSD had not supported in Parliament on September 30. Niculescu seeks to reconcile the parties’ proposals in a governing programme. “There are many good things in all the programmes I have seen so far,” Niculescu said after the consultations. His next task is to reconcile the parties’ proposals into a governing programme, but the initial talks have exposed a fundamental difficulty: agreement on fiscal commitments does not necessarily translate into agreement on the policies required to meet them, or on who should bear responsibility for implementing them. After consultations with PSD, PNL and UDMR, Niculescu is scheduled to meet USR and the other parliamentary groups on Monday, October 12, three days before the deadline for submitting his proposed cabinet to Parliament for an investiture vote.

data.title: Romanians’ crypto holdings estimated at EUR 12 bln amid record participation rate
data.description: Speaking at the opening of the Romanian Fund Managers Summit, Avrămescu, as cited by Ziarul Financiar , stressed that Romania still lacked a designated national authority responsible for supervising crypto-assets, despite the scale of the market. Based on Romania’s population of about 19 million, a 15% ownership rate would represent almost 2.9 million people, according to calculations by Ziarul Financiar. The estimated number of crypto-asset holders exceeds the number of investors in several established domestic investment channels. Intermediaries reported about 325,000 stock market investors at the end of June, according to the Investor Compensation Fund. Romanian open-ended investment funds had more than 1.4 million investors, according to the Association of Fund Administrators (AAF), while the third pillar of the pension system had 1.1 million participants. The mandatory second-pillar pension system had 8.54 million participants. The value of crypto-assets held by Romanians is also comparable with the assets managed by the country’s investment funds. Avrămescu said assets held by all investment funds distributed in Romania reached RON 81 billion, almost 30% above the level recorded at the beginning of the year. The figures presented at the summit point to substantial participation in crypto-assets alongside traditional investment products, while the question of national supervisory responsibility remains unresolved.

data.title: Romania’s power producers Hidroelectrica and Nuclearelectrica hit by drought
data.description: Hidroelectrica is being hit by lower water levels in major rivers, particularly the Danube, while Nuclearelectrica has suspended production for more than a month because of the Danube’s low water level. Hidroelectrica’s adjusted net profit forecast for this year has been cut to RON 3 billion, 16% below the initial budget, reflecting a 4% decline in revenues and a 4% increase in expenses, Economica.net reported. The company’s market capitalisation stands at RON 81 billion, following a 50% rise in its share price over the past year. Nuclearelectrica shares have fallen by 9.2% over the past month and 16.3% over the past six months, although they remain 18.5% higher year on year. The prolonged shutdown of the Cernavodă nuclear power plant has also affected independent electricity suppliers forced to replace contracted volumes with purchases on the wholesale market. Getica 95, Romania’s sixth-largest electricity supplier, filed for insolvency after losing access to electricity it had contracted from Nuclearelectrica and having to purchase replacement volumes on the market, according to Adevarul.ro . The company says it has incurred losses of RON 230 million. Nuclearelectrica had contracted electricity deliveries for this year at approximately RON 550 per MWh. With the expected volumes from Cernavodă unavailable, Getica 95 has had to purchase electricity on the PZUM, Romania’s day-ahead market. Prices during peak hours can frequently reach RON 1,500 per MWh or more.

data.title: Romania’s central bank keeps policy rate at 6.5% and signals higher year-end inflation
data.description: Over a longer horizon, however, the central bank sees “increasingly obvious underlying disinflationary pressures”, primarily from aggregate demand. According to the BNR’s latest assessment, annual inflation is expected to follow an upward trajectory through the end of 2026, mainly due to anticipated increases in fuel, energy and other commodity prices, including agri-food products, amid the prolonged Middle East conflict and this year’s severe drought. Developments in the leu’s exchange rate are another source of inflationary pressure. The central bank’s updated inflation forecast will be released after its November 12 meeting. Erste Group expects the key rate to remain at 6.5% at least until May 2027, as core inflation remains sticky. It forecasted that core inflation will return to the BNR’s target range only in the fourth quarter of 2027. Rate hikes also appear unlikely, unlike in some other economies, given Romania’s deeply negative output gap. Romania’s headline inflation eased to 6.17% y/y in August, partly reflecting base effects following double-digit rates in the first half of the year. The BNR’s latest published forecast, issued in August, envisaged inflation at 6.1% at the end of 2026, falling to 3.8% y/y one year later. Erste said after the latest monetary policy meeting that it planned to raise its year-end inflation forecast from 6.4% to 6.9%, unless September’s reading differs substantially from its expectation of 6.6% y/y. The BNR’s August projection had envisaged inflation of 5.9% y/y in September. On economic growth, the BNR expects positive quarterly growth in Q3, although annual GDP growth is likely to remain negative. The latest data and analyses pointed to an improvement in economic activity compared with the previous quarter, partly reflecting agricultural performance, but also to weaker annual GDP dynamics, with broadly similar developments across the main components of aggregate demand and major economic sectors. Fiscal policy and the Middle East conflict pose risks to the inflation and growth outlook. The central bank highlighted considerable uncertainty surrounding its updated inflation outlook, particularly regarding potential measures to continue fiscal consolidation beyond 2026 in line with the National Medium-Term Fiscal-Structural Plan agreed with the European Commission and the excessive deficit procedure. The Middle East conflict and the associated energy crisis also pose significant risks to economic activity and medium-term inflation. Their effects could be transmitted through consumer purchasing power and confidence, as well as companies’ activity and profitability. The impact on European and global growth and inflation, alongside changes in risk perceptions towards the region, could also affect Romania’s financing costs.

The central bank highlighted considerable uncertainty surrounding its updated inflation outlook, particularly regarding potential measures to continue fiscal consolidation beyond 2026 in line with the National Medium-Term Fiscal-Structural Plan agreed with the European Commission and the excessive deficit procedure. The Middle East conflict and the associated energy crisis also pose significant risks to economic activity and medium-term inflation. Their effects could be transmitted through consumer purchasing power and confidence, as well as companies’ activity and profitability. The impact on European and global growth and inflation, alongside changes in risk perceptions towards the region, could also affect Romania’s financing costs.

data.title: Romania’s new Mintia power plant completes first gas turbine firing, PM says
data.description: The first gas turbine at Romania’s new Mintia power plant ran on natural gas for the first time on Thursday, October 8, interim prime minister Ilie Bolojan announced. The commissioning process will continue with further tests, grid synchronisation, and the delivery of the first electricity to the national power system. “This is an important technical stage for one of Romania’s most significant energy investments in recent years,” Bolojan wrote on Facebook. The project was more than 80% complete when the interim prime minister visited the construction site in June. The installations connecting the turbine to the grid were energised on June 15, according to Ilie Bolojan. The plant’s two gas turbines will have a combined capacity of approximately 1,100 MW. Once the combined cycle is completed, the facility will reach around 1,700 MW of installed capacity. The new plant represents a private investment of more than EUR 1.2 billion and is being built on the site of the former coal-fired Mintia power station. “For Romania, this means more domestically produced energy, fewer imports, and a greater capacity to meet demand during difficult periods, particularly in the evenings and in winter,” prime minister Ilie Bolojan said. He added that the Mintia and Iernut gas-fired plants were expected to strengthen the security of Romania’s electricity system from 2027. “It is essential that all institutions continue to cooperate so that the tests and subsequent stages are completed without further delays,” Bolojan said. https://www.facebook.com/photo/?fbid=1642156663935701&set=a.274245530726828

data.title: Tokyo festival celebrates Romanian pianist Dinu Lipatti
data.description: Dinu Lipatti – Tokyo Music Festival , an event celebrating the Romanian pianist and composer, is scheduled to take place starting this weekend at the Min-On Cultural Centre in Tokyo. The event will bring together musicians Ryugo Yoshino, the Japanese-born pianist who will open the event; tenors Liviu Indricău and Andrei Petre; pianist Constantin Sandu; violinist Diana Jipa and pianist Ștefan Doniga; the Pitești Philharmonic String Quartet; FilJazz & Anita Petruescu; and Doina Argeșului Ensemble. In addition to the music program, the festival covers a documentary exhibition dedicated to the pianist’s life, created with the support of the Dinu Lipatti Memorial House Museum in Fundățeanca, Argeș County. Dinu Lipatti Photo: Romanian Cultural Institute Born into a family of musicians, Lipatti completed his musical training in Bucharest with Florica Musicescu and later in Paris under Alfred Cortot, Paul Dukas and Nadia Boulanger. At 15, he received the Paul Ciuntu Prize at the Bucharest Conservatory. In 1932, he won prizes for his compositions (Piano Sonatina and Sonatina for Violin and Piano) as well as the Grand Prize for his symphonic suite Șătrarii / Les Tziganes . In 1933, at the age of 16, he won the second prize at the International Piano Competition in Vienna. That same year, he won the second prize of the George Enescu Composition Competition. In 1934, he won first prize at the same Enescu competition for Șătrarii . In 1942, he was awarded the Order of Cultural Merit, Knight Class II. His final public concert, a recital in Besançon on September 16, 1950, became legendary: weakened by illness, he ended the recital not with the waltz listed in the program, but with Bach’s Jesus bleibet meine Freude . The festival takes place from October 10 to October 12.

data.title: Romania’s TAIFAS Film Festival brings Balkan cinema, music and culture to Timisoara
data.description: The fourth edition of the TAIFAS Balkan film and culture festival is set to bring films awarded at Cannes, Berlinale, and Sundance, a retrospective dedicated to director Nae Caranfil, and the show “Maria Tănase. A Story” to Timisoara, western Romania. The festival will take place between October 12 and 18. During the seven days of the festival, the program brings together feature films, eight of them in national premiere, two short film programs curated by young people, meetings with directors and actors, film and literature residencies at Cinema Studio 14, as well as shows and events in several venues across the city. The opening of TAIFAS takes place on Monday, October 12, at 19:30, at Cinema Timiș, with "Maria Tănase. A Story," a production of the Constanța State Theater directed by Carmen Lidia Vidu. Mirela Pană plays Maria Tănase, accompanied on piano by George Călin, in a show that brings biography, memory and music into dialogue. After the show, director Carmen Lidia Vidu and actress Mirela Pană will sit down for a chat with Ruxandra Păduraru, a cultural anthropologist who also serves as the festival’s host. The film program opens on Tuesday, October 13, with "The Birthday Party," directed by Miguel Ángel Jiménez, an imaginary biography of tycoon Aristotle Onassis presented in premiere at the Locarno Film Festival, starring Hollywood star Willem Dafoe. Among the films in this edition are "Dreamed Adventure," by Valeska Grisebach, winner this year of the Jury Prize at Cannes, "Nina Roza," by Geneviève Dulude-de Celles, awarded the Silver Bear for Best Screenplay at Berlinale 2026, as well as two titles awarded at this year’s Sundance festival, namely "Shame and Money" by Visar Morina and "Hold Onto Me" by Myrsini Aristidou, this year’s Cyprus entry for the Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film. The selection made by artistic director Cătălin Olaru also includes two films from the 2026 edition of the Karlovy Vary festival, namely "Small-Time Crooks," by Mate Ugrin, awarded the FIPRESCI Prize, and "Almost a Whole Person," by Efthimis Kosemund-Sanidis, awarded for direction in the Proxima section. The TAIFAS 2026 selection is completed by one of the star titles from the Sarajevo Film Festival, namely "17," by Kosara Mitić, which centers on the friendship of two teenage girls confronted with sexual violence and was awarded the Audience Award and the Best Actress award. The screenings will be accompanied by conversations with festival guests. The public will meet directors Nikola Ležaić, Mate Ugrin and Efthimis Kosemund-Sanidis, as well as actresses Yana Radeva and Flomaria Papadaki. Similarly, the screening of "Shame and Money," scheduled for the closing of the festival, will also be followed by a Zoom discussion with director Visar Morina. Among the main events of this edition is the retrospective dedicated to director Nae Caranfil. "E pericoloso sporgersi" (1993), "Filantropica" (2002) and "The Rest Is Silence" (2007) offer three perspectives closely linked to this year’s festival theme: the desire to escape from the final years of communism, the mechanisms of imposture during the transition and the beginnings of Romanian cinema. All screenings will be followed by Q&A sessions with filmmaker Nae Caranfil, who will also hold a masterclass on October 18, from 15:30, in the Small Hall of Cinema Studio. The festival includes the Film Residency program for young filmmakers, the Literary Residency program, including book launches, colloquia, reading clubs, and Through the Balkans with Pork, a gastronomic journey through Romania, Serbia, Croatia, Bulgaria, North Macedonia, and beyond.

data.title: Romanian companies can access EUR 7.55 mln in total funding through System EU
data.description: Companies and organizations in Romania can access EUR 7.55 million through the European SystemEU project, the Ministry of Economy, Digitalization, Entrepreneurship and Tourism (MEDAT) announced. The call is open until November 16, 2026. As part of it, entities from across the country can access funding of up to EUR 2.2 million for projects that take digital solutions from the prototype stage to market launch. Between five and eight projects will be selected under three funding thresholds, namely small projects (up to EUR 750,000), medium-level projects (up to EUR 1.1 million, with consortia of 3-5 entities from at least three participating regions, mandatorily including a research organization and a company), as well as flagship projects – up to EUR 2.2 million, with consortia of 5-8 entities from all five SystemEU regions, established according to the Triple Helix model, bringing together at least one research organization, a company and a public authority or a public sector organization. “The selected projects will develop, test and validate digital solutions in real-life conditions, starting from a minimum level of technological maturity, from a functional prototype, already tested in realistic conditions, and reaching a completed and validated solution, ready for the market or for real use,” the same source added. The ministry specified that the targeted areas are Health – digital health and medical technologies (digital health & medtech); Energy – decentralized, clean and smart energy networks; Mobility – intelligent transport and logistics systems. “Funding rates are up to 100% for start-ups, 70% for SMEs, 50% for large enterprises and 100% for public bodies, NGOs and research organizations. Individual entities can participate in several projects, but the total funding received for all selected projects in which they are part of the consortium cannot exceed EUR 600,000, according to the FSPT funding mechanism. The projects will run for a period of between 15 and 18 months, with implementation scheduled to begin in February-March 2027,” the Ministry noted. All information about the call and application submission can be found on the official FSTP portal, while to support applicants in forming interregional consortia that meet the eligibility criteria, the project provides access to a dedicated online database, designed to facilitate the establishment of partnerships. Candidates can register, publish concrete project proposals, and view other profiles registered on the Open Hubs SYSTEMEU community platform. SystemEU is a project funded through the Horizon Europe Program (European Innovation Ecosystems), running from January 1, 2025 to December 31, 2028, with a total estimated budget of approximately EUR 14.87 million. The project connects universities, research organizations, companies, public authorities, and innovation stakeholders from five European regions – Bavaria (Germany), Northwestern Romania, Castilla y Leon (Spain), Tuzla Canton (Bosnia and Herzegovina) and the Norte Region (Portugal), to reduce territorial innovation gaps, strengthening competitiveness and accelerating digital transformation in health, energy and mobility.

data.title: Wonderful appoints Yannis Jacob-Drăghici GM for Romania and Moldova
data.description: Enterprise AI software company Wonderful appointed Yannis Jacob-Drăghici as general manager for Romania and Moldova. He will oversee the company’s operations in both markets and work with large organisations on adopting artificial intelligence across their businesses, Revistabiz.ro reported. Wonderful provides software infrastructure through which companies can develop, test, deploy, and manage AI agents and applications. Its clients operate in sectors including telecommunications, banking and financial services, media, healthcare, and retail. The company said that it plans to target AI applications in customer support, sales, back-office operations, human resources, and engineering in Romania and Moldova. “As AI models become more accessible, the question for companies is no longer whether the technology works, but how quickly they can turn it into measurable business value,” Yannis Jacob-Drăghici said. He added that implementing AI across an organisation required companies to redesign processes, connect the technology to existing data and systems, and manage changes affecting employees’ roles and working methods. Wonderful completed a USD 550 million Series C funding round in September 2026 at a valuation of USD 5 billion. Insight Partners led the round, with participation from Salesforce and existing investors Index Ventures, IVP, Vine Ventures, 9Yards, and Bessemer Venture Partners. The company operates in more than 35 markets and has over 800 employees worldwide.

data.title: DSP o Maquiavélico Ganancioso
data.description: Guineenses, mais uma vez, venho para vos alertar sobre o perigo que Domingos Simões Pereira representa para a Guiné-Bissau. Faço esse alerta a todos os guineenses sem exceção que se encontre no país ou no estrangeiro, ao PAIGC em especial e na pessoa do Cipriano Cassamá em concreto. Alerta esse sobre o verdadeiro DSP, o verdadeiro espírito que move esse sujeito, o qual alguns ainda continuam a acreditar para não dizer adorar. Domingos Simões Pereira é um manipulador, um verdadeiro chantagista e calculista provavelmente, tipo de comportamento que ultrapassa o nível de psicopata. U m ambicioso desmedido, um verdadeiro criminoso que sabe como e quando cometer o crime. Ele jamais coabitaria não só com JOMAV, assim como com qualquer presidente que seria eleito, a não ser o que ele apoiou disfarçadamente. Isto porque ele tem sua própria agenda, e o PAIGC é simplesmente uma plataforma para sua concretização. DSP jamais coabitaria com JOMAV porque o seu candidato preferido era o Paulo Gomes e sempre será, o qual juntamente com Tchitchi vão delineando mecanismo de modo a serem os novos donos da Guiné-Bissau. Segundo eles este é um processo a médio prazo, e é preciso coragem e paciência para concretiza-lo. Ganhar o congresso não importa em que circunstância e ter novamente o partido na mão, é uma fase concluída em proveito deles, enquanto verdadeiros militantes do PAIGC estão a bater palmas. Depois dessa eleição legislativa, não importa o resultado, o Cipriano Cassama que se prepare a mala ou fica de bico fechado, pois o candidato preferido para o partido será o Paulo Gomes, e esse sim deve ter a voz dentro do partido. DSP é um ambicioso desmedido, nunca teve consideração por ninguém, JOMAV muito menos, o sujeito é um maquiavélico nato, Cipriano Casama será descartado quando menos esperar podes tomar a nota. Guineenses, falar do Paulo Gomes e Tchitchi é falar do MCCI e demais outras organizações e personalidades camufladas no nosso país. Esses dois indivíduos são os principais financiadores do MCCI e demais outras personalidades boca de aluguel na cidade de Bissau. O MCCI, Milícia idealizado por JBV e DSP, agora financiado e dirigido por "futuro triângulo do poder" ou seja, "DSP, Paulo Gomes e Tchitchi", têm 3 principais objectivos: 1º Perturbar a ordem pública em nome da cidadania, difamar e tentar descredibilizar qualquer que seja organizações ou indivíduos não alinhados ao triângulo, de modo a suportar suas caminhadas na busca do poder. 2º Caso se concretize o objectivo do triângulo, o papel da Milícia do MCCI passará a ser de vigilância constante a todos os adversários de modo a garantir falsa paz social e o poder de controlo. 3º Tentar ganhar credibilidade junto das organizações internacionais e regionais, através de suas visitas e actividades de fachada, para quando houver as tais actividades de perturbações de ordem pública, poderem ganhar notoriedade. Mas isso não deve preocupar ninguém, pois estão bem identificados e bem caçados, dentro e fora da Guiné-Bissau. Não tenho nada contra ninguém, mas quem continuar a perturbar verdadeira paz social dos guineenses em troca de benefícios como sempre foi nos últimos anos dessa crise, e que sempre tenho tolerado, então que fique claro "estou firme e determinado para tudo e todos". Para finalizar, gostaria de vos deixar uma reflexão com a seguinte frase: " Domingos Simões Pereira é um perigo grave para o futuro do país ". Isto porque publicar aqui tudo que é necessário para provar ou sustentar a razão dessa frase, só pode agravar ainda mais a paz social que tanto necessitamos. Chega, chega não podemos continuar a viver nessa turbulência vida toda, meus irmãos guineenses, não é saudável, é tóxico, não é justo para um povo que tanto sofreu. António Aly Silva » aaly.silva@gmail.com » aaly_silva@hotmail.com » Tel. (+245) 668 31 13

data.title: APANHA-SE MAIS DEPRESSA UM MENTIROSO QUE UM COXO!
data.description:
DSP através da sua equipa de "Lambe-Botas" está cavando cada vez mais a sua própria cova, adiantando cada vez mais o seu fim. Somente alguns acreditavam que foi ele quem estava por trás do "Progresso Nacional" o blog onde começou toda essa história de Mentiras, Calunias, Difamações, Ameaças e tantos outros agressões tóxicas ao espírito humano, a todos os que não estão do seu lado e cujo o único objectivo, era ser chamado de rei dos réis da Guiné. Comandou o Progresso Nacional assim como Bin Laden comandou a Al-Qaeda e acabou por fracassar. Pensou, repensou e resolveu voltar novamente ainda com mais TERROR e está a comandar o Guiné Puro tentando levar toda a nação ao abismo assim como o ISIS quer levar a humanidade. Camaradas, Guiné Puro assim como o falecido Progresso Nacional é o reflexo do espirito de DSP, alí é possivel ver tudo e quanto o sujeito é baixo. DSP é um hipócrita e um anarquista moderno. "ACHAS QUE AS NOSSAS MARCHAS SÃO RESULTADO DE VENDAS E COMPRAS?!" essa foi uma das frases da recente publicação que mostram por quem e para que fim, é dirigido o Guiné Puro ou melhor o blog do terror como podem ver já a seguir. Demonstraram mais uma vez claramente que o "MCCI" pertence a DPS, pois uma publicação dessa no próprio blog do ganancioso só pode ser das duas uma: "Boca capli elis ou Foronta passanta e dicidi ca sucundi rostu". Camaradas, Domingos Simões Pereira afundou seu próprio barco devido a sua ganância e complexo de superioridade. "I pirigu pa i faladu ba cuma, el i unicu alguim cu bai escola na Guiné" seu ultimo desejo é "afundar com todos, inclusive o PAIGC". __________PARA A VOSSA CONFIRMAÇÃO, AQUI ESTÁ A PUBLICAÇÃO_________ MARCOS GALINA BARBOSA VAI PERCEBER QUE METEU COM GENTE
PERSISTENTE. BÔ DISSAL I NA BIN FASSI PASSSAÇÃO LI. tUDO PUBLICAÇÕES KU I FASSI
I NA RESP+UNDI PAREL. NIN IKANA SEDU DIDIA. NONA VINGAL MANERA KU NÓ PUDI. JÁ
TEMOS ALGUÉM NO AEROPORTO PARA NOS INFOMAR O DIA EM QUE EL CHEGAR. INVENTOU
AGRESSÃO E NESTE MOMENTO ESTÁ EM QUELUZ EM PORTUGAL. FILHO DA PUTA. MENTIROSO
COMO OS TEUS PATRÕES OS SUJOS JOMAV E BRAIMA CAMARÁ. MARCOS GALINA, BU NA
ARREPENDI. PERA BU DJUBI. ACHAS QUE AS NOSSAS MARCHAS SÃO RESULTADO DE VENDAS E
COMPRAS?! VAMOS PROVAR DEPOIS. FIDJU DI BALETA Olá a todos, ainda bem que descobriram
que o Pirata informático- hackec é o Marcos Galina Barbosa, Eng. Informático.
Tentei várias vezes avisar o Ticha Aly Silva mas ele não respondeu e nem deu
importância julgo eu. No tempo da campanha para a liderança do Paigc, este
indivíduo era um fervoroso apoiante do Bá Quecuto no Facebook e a técnica que
usava era o envio de Phishing aos apoiantes do Dsp, recolhia informações
pessoais das pessoas que posteriormente eram expostas no Blog do Doka. Tentou
comigo mas não resultou. Tenham cuidado com este sujeito que está nas mãos de
B. Camara. Outra coisa, gostaria de conhecer a vossa página no Fecebook. Estamos Juntos. AC Nota GP: Até jovens inocentes,
Lesmes, Masta Tito e demais outros, os tais vendidos e comprados foram as tuas
vítimas. teu filho da puta que o bandido de Baciro Djá trouxe para Bissau para funções no aparelho de Estado e dizes que outros recebem favores.
Desde quando é que és mais honesto ou
mais competentes que os outros? Pagas e até pode ser com a tua vida para
perceberes as irresponsabilidades
dos teus actos. Publicada por O

data.title: DSP, UM PERIGO GRAVE PARA FUTURO DO PAÍS
data.description: Os meios de comunicação também são as formas de manipulação mais utilizadas pelos poderes políticos, dado o seu impacto social. As informações são manipuladas não apenas tendo em vista omitir factos relevantes, mas também distorcer o conteúdo da informação veiculada, produzir ou forjar a opinião pública, de modo que a mesma se ajuste às ideias dos gananciosos. A única forma dos cidadãos evitarem cair nestes processos de manipulação é tornarem-se mais vigilantes em relação às instituições democráticas e aos órgãos de informação, adoptando uma atitude de permanente reflexão crítica sobre a informação que lhes é fornecida. Na Guiné-Bissau, nos últimos anos, cresceu exponencialmente o número de pessoas mediocres, pessoas sem escrúpulos ligadas à produção de rádios e outros meios de comunicação com influencia na nossa sociedade, gente que apesar da sua enorme influência na sociedade, trabalha na mais completa impunidade e sem qualquer controlo ético/democrático. Obcecado pelo poder, ciente da dificuldade do povo guineense em avaliar informações, ciente do poder dos instrumentos de comunicação, Domingos Simões Pereira (DSP) nunca menosprezou esses instrumentos para atingir seu objectivo, sempre usou-os de forma desonesta como agora está a fazer tudo por tudo para manter no controlo desses veicúlos, mesmo que isso custe a vida dos outros. Governou na corrupção, no nepotismo e no desvios de somas astronómicas do dinheiro de povo, que muito serviria para investimentos na saúde, educação e outros serviços publicos, para beneficiar familiares e amigos. Finge que preocupa com os problemas do país, mas só engana o povo honesto, humilde e trabalhador que infelizmente sofre muito, não sei até quando, devido a sua paciência e tolerância aos governantes como DSP, criminoso travestido em politico que vive na custa de povo e acima de tudo ainda fa-lo refem do próprio suor. Roubou e decepcionou tanto não só aos guineenses assim como a comunidade internacional que sempre acreditou que o sujeito era ideal para ajudar esse povo a sair do ciclo de sofrimento que parece infinito. Foi demitido, não conformou e está a fazer tudo na medida do possível para continuar a complicar a vida dos guineenses. Razão disso é que depois de perder a batalha nos meios de comunicações mais modernos nomeadamente os blogues onde investiu grandes somas do dinheiro de povo, para fazer a lavagem cerebral dos menos instruídos e não só. Fugiu do facebook onde sempre frequentava e comunicava com todos tentado passar a mensagem de um politico moderno e aberto a diálogo/opiniões, mas que afinal era simplesmente um falso modernista. Caiu a mascara e já não consegue enganar ninguem, pois a sua credibilidade está abaixo de zero, para não dizer outra coisa. Camaradas, para conhecimento geral, com o dinheiro roubado que custou suor de povo guineense, DSP decidiu avançar com um outro novo plano maquiavelico, para criar a sua própria estação de rádio. Documento António Aly Silva » aaly.silva@gmail.com » aaly_silva@hotmail.com » Tel. (+245) 668 31 13

data.title: DSP não respeita os antigos combatentes e sempre usou e abusou desses camaradas. Prova disso é que continuou a governar mesmo já com Carlos Correia como primeiro ministro.
